The gate is line-local rg regex and can be bypassed by code that actually compiles. Blocking bypasses to close:
B1 use bitty_ai_runtime::tool; (module import with no trailing ::) passes.
B2 use bitty_ai_runtime::tool as core_tool; then core_tool::ToolRegistry passes.
B3 use bitty_ai_runtime :: tool :: ToolRegistry; and multiline use paths pass.
B4 Renaming the Cargo dependency to core-runtime makes use core_runtime::tool::ToolRegistry; pass every hard-coded pattern. Derive the crate name from Cargo.toml instead of hard-coding it.
B5 Nested grouped imports plus impl<T> ModelProvider for LocalProvider<T> pass.
B6 unsafe /* comment */ { and a newline between unsafe and { pass.
B7 The design explicitly forbids binding references to FakeToolExecutor but the name is absent from the patterns; bitty_ai_runtime::tool::FakeToolExecutor passed.
B8 An allowlist entry naming a literal file with brace syntax, src/{lib.rs,allowed.rs}, is accepted and its glob excludes unrelated files. Allowlist entries must be exact paths, never globs or brace expansions.
B9 rg neither follows nor rejects symlinks; a #[path] source symlink followed by Cargo containing a banned reference passes, and a symlink loop passes silently.
B10 Crate discovery examines only immediate, non-dot shell-globbed crates/* entries; explicit workspace members at crates/.bitty-ai-lua and bindings/bitty-ai-lua pass. Discover members from the workspace manifest rather than a glob.

Do not weaken the gate into a best-effort check. The design mandates fail-closed. {"description":"Priority: P1 | Area: area:ai-runtime | Labels: fix,P1 | Milestone: v0.1.0 | Task: AI-0152 | Second fix round for the AI-0145 lint gate after round-2 review returned NEEDS-FIX (PX-0593, checkpoint 01M3CA4E68V52PDRRKDP20SESR).

Read the round-2 findings in full first. Work on branch ctx-ai-0145/feat-lint-gate in worktree .worktrees/ctx-ai-0145-feat-lint-gate, on top of 0446724. B1-B7 and B9 are closed; five blocking classes remain, all demonstrated by the reviewer with compiling fixtures:

1. Local macro-mediated Core paths bypass the gate. A local macro_rules! that expands to a Core type path, pub use, module alias, or dyn trait object compiles and exits 0, because the crate identifier is not adjacent to :: in the pre-expansion text. This is NOT covered by the accepted external-macro-expansion residual: the macro and the Core identifier are both local binding source. Treat local macro definitions that mention the Core crate name as a rejection class.

2. Ordinary compiler-reachable source escapes the scanned tree. All of these compile with banned references while the gate exits 0: #[path = ...] mod, include!(...), a Cargo [lib] path pointing outside the binding directory, and Cargo source placed under an excluded target/ directory. The gate must validate Cargo target src_path values and follow the textual #[path]/include! source graph at least one level, or reject such constructs outright in binding crates. The round-2 reviewer judged the external-#[path] residual NOT acceptable and blocking, because ordinary binding source escaping defeats the stated purpose that every future binding crate is born inside the gate.

3. Whole-file allowlisting permits cross-file laundering. An allowlisted file may define pub type Alias = bitty_ai_runtime::tool::ToolRegistry; and a non-allowlisted file may use that alias; everything compiles and the gate exits 0. The exact-path mechanism is unsound as an enforcement boundary because an allowlisted file becomes an unchecked capability-export surface. Require a construct-specific exception that cannot re-export, or an equivalent non-exporting invariant.

4. Excluded local path dependencies escape classification. A binding crate can depend on an in-repository helper listed in workspace.exclude; the helper references Core and re-exports an alias; the binding uses the alias; cargo check succeeds and the gate exits 0. Classify local path dependencies, not just workspace members.

5. Empty binding set passes. The gate returns 0 for BINDING_PATHS=(), which conflicts with the fail-closed criterion and needs an explicit authority decision, because the design document expects zero binding crates on the pre-binding tree. Do not silently change this either way: record the conflict, pick the option that preserves fail-closed while remaining compatible with the bootstrap tree, and document the bootstrap exception explicitly.

Also extend scripts/tests/host-boundary-lint-test.sh with a regression case for each of the five classes; the round-2 reviewer judged the suite sound but incomplete for exactly these.

Accepted residuals that may stay, but must remain explicitly documented: external macro expansion, generated/build-script/OUT_DIR source, and comment/string false positives.

The design's textual approach has now failed twice against compiling bypasses. If you conclude it cannot be made sound, say so plainly and propose the narrowest sound alternative as a separate proposal; do not silently ship a gate that only catches common spellings. Do NOT introduce the HostBoundary trait, migrate call sites, or close AIQ-31. Run just check, just typecheck, shellcheck -S warning, shfmt -d, actionlint, act -n, and gitleaks. {"content":"NEEDS-FIX (1 blocking, 5 non-blocking). Commit a7981dc on ctx-AI-0151-fix-toolbus-attribution (base 58f9d5b, worktree clean, no untracked). Independently re-derived: the classification, the exhaustiveness, the caller set, the disposition coherence, and all three mutations.

BLOCKING F1 — stale and now-false adapter contract, tool.rs:664-668 and :684-686. ToolExecutor::execute # Errors still reads 'Return ToolError::Denied when the host refuses, or ToolError::EffectUnknown when the effect may have happened but acknowledgement was lost. Other errors propagate as bus failures.' That is the PRE-change contract: post-change no error propagates as a bus failure (dispatch returns Err on no path, tool.rs:1029). It is also the exact place where the adapter obligation the whole classification rests on must live, and it states neither. tool.rs is in the authorized scope. Failure scenario: a network tool adapter author reads only this contract, issues the request, and returns a request-shaped variant (e.g. ArgumentsTooLarge) to report a remote rejection; the bus records Failed (retry-safe, no reconcile, tool.rs:1167-1170/1196) and the Agent continues the turn, so the model retries and the adapter re-issues the request — a double apply with no Unknown and no reconcile obligation. Pre-change that adapter produced a turn-failing Err. Fix: rewrite both # Errors blocks to state the contract — a request-shaped variant is a bus-owned pre-dispatch fact (TB-3, ai-architecture.md:949: 'Every ToolCall is validated against the registry before any host dispatch'); an adapter that has issued the request MUST use EffectUnknown; every other post-contact error is classified Unknown by the bus. Non-blocking F1b (tool.rs:1133-1136): the same rationale sentence in the classification comment is factually wrong — 'A conformant adapter raises them before issuing the outbound request' cannot be true, because the bus itself raises InvalidName/UnknownTool/ArgumentsTooLarge (authorize_call tool.rs:911-924) and CallLimitExceeded (tool.rs:1044-1052) pre-contact, and DuplicateTool/DescriptionTooLarge/SchemaTooLarge/RegistryFull are ToolRegistry::register-time facts never raised on the dispatch path. Cite TB-3 plus the EffectUnknown obligation instead.

SECURITY ASSESSMENT of the rule. The DIRECTION is task-authorized (AI-0151: 'Do not blanket-map everything to Unknown either; a deterministic local failure after contact is Failed') and I do not contest it. Two findings a reviewer must carry forward. (a) Yes, a misbehaving or malicious adapter CAN force a blind retry: it performs a side-effecting remote call, then returns any of the eight request-shaped variants; the bus grants Failed — determinate, 'a retry carries no double-apply risk' — the Agent continues (agent.rs:790-853), the model reads 'failed: {reason}' (agent.rs:1016) and retries, and the adapter re-issues. No Unknown, no ExecOutcome::Unknown, no reconcile. Blast radius is bounded to one turn (<=8 calls by MAX_TOOL_CALLS_PER_TURN, <=32 by MAX_EXECUTIONS_PER_AGENT) and a Completed session refuses a further run_turn (SessionError::AlreadyTerminated), so it is not unbounded. (b) The rule buys nothing in the conformant case and only ever fires in the non-conformant one: all eight Failed-bucket variants are either already enforced pre-contact by the bus or not dispatch-time errors at all, so the Failed arm is provably unreachable for a bus-conformant call. Non-blocking F2 (recommendation): the bus can close the trust hole with locally verifiable state it already holds — at tool.rs:1151, downgrade to Unknown any request-shaped claim the bus can disprove (e.g. ArgumentsTooLarge when call.arguments.len() <= MAX_TOOL_ARGUMENTS_BYTES, which authorize_call has already proven). No blanket-Unknown required.

EXHAUSTIVENESS: VERIFIED. No wildcard arm. Independent probe: added ToolError::Probe and cargo check produced three E0004 non-exhaustive-pattern errors, including 'Err(ToolError::Probe) not covered' at tool.rs:1061 (the dispatch match) — so a new variant cannot ship unclassified. All 12 existing variants are bucketed: Denied and EffectUnknown on their own pre-existing arms, 8 to Failed, 2 to Unknown; none reaches a default. Probe reverted, tree byte-identical to a7981dc.

MUTATIONS: all three independently reproduced. Bare-Err reversion: 2 conformance tests + 3 tool unit tests fail. Blanket-Unknown: request_shaped_executor_error_is_attributed_as_a_determinate_failure + 2 tool unit tests + generic_executor_error_is_bounded_in_the_failed_record fail. Blanket-Failed: generic_executor_error_is_attributed_for_reconciliation + post_contact_response_shaped_errors_are_unknown_statuses_to_reconcile fail. All reverted.

DISPOSITION / DATA COHERENCE: COHERENT, no consumer misled. Consumers of ResultDisposition exhaustively: agent.rs:811 (is_rejection -> only Rejected fails the turn), agent.rs:813-818 (typed cause extraction from Rejected), agent.rs:866 (the now-dead Err arm), lib.rs:151 (re-export). adoption.rs:317 check_adoption reads record.status only and never disposition. Consumers of ToolExecution::is_untrusted_surface: none in production src — agent.rs:989 hardcodes true on the derived ContextRecord rather than reading the bus value, so true is the fail-safe direction and no consumer branches on it. Accepted-with-empty-data is coherent and precedented: the Denied (1115), EffectUnknown (1101) and refused() (1244) records already set Accepted with Vec::new(), and the doc update at tool.rs:567-573 accurately describes that. Note the Accepted choice is LOAD-BEARING, not cosmetic: it is what lets the turn continue. No consumer treats Accepted as 'payload validated and present'.

normalized() + bound_reason: CORRECT, an improvement, no double-bounding regression. bound_reason (bridge.rs:119) is per-byte scrub to printable ASCII plus truncate to MAX_REASON_BYTES=512, hence idempotent, so applying normalized() then bound_reason is one effective bound, not a double truncation. It is strictly wider coverage than before: previously only the Agent's Err arm (agent.rs:859) normalized, and only EffectUnknown/Denied reasons were bounded at the bus (tool.rs:1099, 1113). Note for the corpus, not a defect: the post-contact Failed/Unknown reason is adapter-controlled text disclosed to the model, bounded but not authority-bearing — the same exposure Denied already has.

CALLER AUDIT: VERIFIED. live_host.rs:414 and :436 are ToolDispatchService::dispatch and ExecutionService::dispatch — the fields are declared tools: ToolDispatchService and executions: ExecutionService (live_host.rs:154-155) from bitty_ipc, and the method signatures are unrelated to ToolBus::dispatch. The only production ToolBus::dispatch caller in the workspace is agent.rs:788; harness.rs:272 and local_provider.rs:2416 construct a ToolBus but never dispatch. agent.rs:854-868 IS genuinely dead: dispatch's two early returns are Ok (1042, 1045), and the match at 1059 covers Ok plus all 12 Err variants with Ok bodies — Err is unreachable. Confirmed empirically: under the bare-Err reversion probe that arm became reachable and generic_executor_error_is_bounded_in_the_failed_record failed; under the committed code it is not. Leaving it is untidy, not a defect; non-blocking F3 — record a follow-up to migrate the signature to ToolExecution and delete the arm.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE: CLEAN apart from the flagged exception. Exactly three files modified vs 58f9d5b, all M, no additions: crates/bitty-ai-runtime/src/tool.rs, crates/bitty-ai-runtime/tests/diagnostic_normalization.rs, crates/bitty-ai-slice/tests/network_tool_conformance.rs. No Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock change, no new dependency, no network I/O or socket, no AIQ-33/AIQ-36 closure, no audit vocabulary in the diff, no CI or manifest change. Worktree clean with zero untracked files; cbccb41 is an ancestor of a7981dc; origin/main cbccb41 unchanged.

FLAGGED ITEM 1 (forced scope extension, diagnostic_normalization.rs:168): RIGHT CALL, should NOT have been a separate task, but the process was wrong. Substantively correct: the test's premise was the removed bare-Err path, it was the only failing workspace test, and leaving it red would have violated the AGENTS.md mandatory-gate rule; splitting it would have meant a knowingly-red tree. The edit did NOT weaken the subject — it still pins AI-RUN-008 bounding of the classified Failed reason and now also pins the new turn outcome, which makes the behavior change explicit and reviewable. One honest weakening to record (non-blocking F4, diagnostic_normalization.rs:168): the original asserted display-safety of the name inside the typed AgentError; the new form asserts only the reason, and because the outer bound_reason would scrub the hostile name anyway, the test no longer distinguishes ToolError::normalized() from the outer bound — acceptable, since the outer guard is the one that protects the disclosed string. Also non-blocking: the test name 'generic_executor_error_...' is now stale, since 'generic executor error' is no longer a category. Process finding, non-blocking F5: the extension was decided unilaterally and reported in a progress note after the fact; the commander should have been asked for a scope expansion before the commit, not informed after it.

FLAGGED ITEM 2 (agent behavior change): SAFE, and the 'continue then' direction is defensible — with one caveat a caller must not misread. Trace: Failed reaches agent.rs:790, is neither is_admission_refusal (796) nor is_rejection (811), sets unknown=false and denied=false (821-822), is recorded by record_execution (825) which pushes an ExecutionRecord with Failed plus a ContextRecord holding empty inline data (agent.rs:966-975), is disclosed to the model as 'failed: {reason}' (agent.rs:1016), is rendered to the sink as a ToolCard 'status=failed' (agent.rs:907), and then the loop continues. The turn's FINAL outcome does NOT reflect the failure: if the next round carries no tool calls the turn returns ExecOutcome::Completed and the session is finished non-failed (agent.rs:730-742). So 'Completed' can now mean 'a tool deterministically failed and the model then narrated completion'. I judge that acceptable, because the failure is not lost — it is in agent.executions() (public getter, agent.rs:468), in the emitted ToolCard, and in the model's own context — and because ToolStatus::Failed is already the canonical known/no-effect/non-quarantined terminal used by the reconcile seam (agent.rs:1264, 1347) and by adoption.rs:485, where a Failed record adopts as a plain non-quarantined effect. Every pre-change non-Success outcome terminated the turn, so this is a genuinely new semantic, and it is the one behavior change a consumer of ExecOutcome could be surprised by; no such consumer exists in this repo. Crucially, the security-relevant refusals stay fail-closed: authorization and Inspect-tier denial remain Refused (agent.rs:796-803), payload rejection remains Rejected -> fail (811-820), and Denied still fails (840-852). Non-blocking F6: this deserves an explicit corpus sentence that a determinate post-contact failure is non-terminal for the turn and that a host must read agent.executions() rather than infer tool success from ExecOutcome::Completed.

FLAGGED ITEM 3 (no docs sync): GENUINE SEPARATE-REPOSITORY CONSTRAINT, confirmed. bitty-ai-docs is a separate repo mounted at docs/ as a submodule (bitty-ai/.gitmodules url github.com/bitty-terminal/bitty-ai-docs, pin ac26f99); the worktree has it uninitialized, and the canonical material is not editable from bitty-ai. Shape: new table pending_effects in bitty-ai-session (NOT slice): CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pending_effects (call_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, session_id TEXT NOT NULL, task_id TEXT, tool TEXT NOT NULL, args_digest TEXT, status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open', disposition TEXT, generation INTEGER NOT NULL, epoch INTEGER NOT NULL, begun_at_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, resolved_at_ms INTEGER) + index on (session_id, status). Follows sessions.rs ensure_table/session_bindings precedent (additive migration, pre-AI-0199 files gain table on first call). Single-txn atomicity: begin and resolve each run in one transaction on the shared single-writer Connection (claim_writer_fast discipline, content_store.rs:577); begin+resolve are SEPARATE txns (crash between them is the point — the open row must survive); resolve does UPDATE status+disposition+resolved_at then DELETE in the SAME txn (resolve-time delete; no tombstone — table is not content-addressed history, it is a live set; retention = zero resolved rows retained, disposition returned to caller before delete). WriterBusy: map DatabaseBusy/DatabaseLocked -> typed WriterBusy/Storage(WRITER_BUSY_MSG) exactly like sessions.rs:241-257 + content_store.rs:468-496; busy_timeout ZERO fail-fast on open (wheel_kernel.rs open_with_config), 5000ms steady-state (DURABLE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS). Core equivalent/duplicate check
--------------------------------
No equivalent landed work was found in Core history or current files. #2127 supplies only resident opaque stdio framing and restart fences; #2184 supplies only generic Core snapshot version injection/local acknowledgement. Neither authenticates Core origin, publishes the accepted provider-routing bytes, receives a remote ack, binds a channel/session proof, or invalidates proof on helper replacement. The AI-0324 endpoint/projection is helper-side only and strict remains Unbound.

2. Smallest A/B design alternatives (recommendation, not a ruling)
====================================================================
A — Keep the resident stdio pair and make it an explicit launch-bound control/data channel (recommended candidate for design review)
- Treat the Core-created duplex pipe pair plus the Core launch record (resolved executable + verified digest + local helper generation) as the channel authority. Do not infer authority from fields in the JSON payload. Add an accepted control-plane handshake/record type on the existing bounded framed stream, or an explicitly separated inherited control fd if mixing control and 13 request frames is rejected by review. The exact record type/fields are deliberately not chosen here.
- Core sends the publication only after the helper-side channel handshake is live; helper returns an ack only on the same current channel. Core accepts an ack only when its private pending publication, current helper generation, and channel instance all match. The helper issues proof only after consuming the exact pending ack and comparing its own registry projection.
- Why smallest: no listener, socket discovery, generic IPC registry, MCP path, provider I/O, or credentials in Core; it reuses the already bounded stdio/framing and current generation fence.
- Actual risks requiring security review: anonymous pipes do not expose SO_PEERCRED; a same-user process that somehow obtains a duplicated/inherited fd would be indistinguishable without a stronger platform mechanism; helper executable replacement, fd inheritance/handle leakage, crash/restart races, Windows handle semantics, and control/data interleaving need explicit tests. The launch digest and private inherited channel reduce these risks but are not a claim that same-user process identity alone authenticates Core.

B — Introduce an OS-authenticated local control endpoint (Unix domain socket / Windows named pipe) for publication control, retaining the existing stdio stream for ordinary ai.* requests
- Core and helper connect through a dedicated endpoint and use existing peer-credential/ACL style authentication plus a per-connection channel/generation binding; helper accepts publication only on that authenticated control connection. Existing bounded frame/wire rules can be reused only where the accepted design says so.
- Why stronger: OS peer credentials/ACLs provide a reviewed transport identity and endpoint replacement checks beyond self-asserted metadata. It gives a natural recheck/revocation point.
- Actual risks/costs: new endpoint lifecycle/discovery and cleanup, platform parity (the consumed auth pin documents Windows verification as an explicit unsupported result), path/ACL/symlink races, extra transport and test surface, possible resident-helper startup deadlock, and a second channel to coordinate with stdio generation. It must not become generic client RPC or a provider registry authority.

Recommendation for the next design review: compare A and B, with A as the minimal bounded candidate only if the security review accepts launch-bound private-channel possession plus digest-verified spawn as sufficient Core-origin authentication. Otherwise reject A and require B (or another explicitly accepted authenticated mechanism). Do not implement either from this note; the current CTX-0161 acceptance grants no choice.

3. Exact bounded lifecycle and transport needs
===============================================
The design must specify these abstract events without guessing a new ai.* method:

1. Channel establishment: Core starts one digest-verified helper generation; a channel-bound handshake establishes the authorized Core/helper channel and protocol version. Missing, malformed, wrong-version, timeout, or wrong-channel handshake fails closed. The handshake must not use caller-echoed provider metadata as its proof.
2. Initial publish: Core obtains the exact accepted provider-routing canonical bytes from the approved credential-free metadata source, mints a never-reused publication identity and strictly increasing Core version, and sends one bounded publication on the authenticated current channel. 5. Equality proof: helper consumes the exact pending ack, compares its current populated ProviderRegistry projection byte-for-byte/digest-for-digest, and issues an opaque proof. The proof is helper-created, non-forgeable in the helper process, scoped to publication identity/domain/version/digest plus current registry revision/publication epoch, and carries no mutation authority.
6. Strict use: only after proof is current may a separately authorized strict `ai.provider_list` path proceed. The existing 13 methods and their schemas stay as-is unless a future accepted wire design explicitly changes one. In particular, generic `snapshot_version` remains a correlator and does not become publication identity; no new `ai.publish`, `ai.ack`, or similar method is proposed here.

Core's source-view mutation invalidates its pending/ack state and requires a fresh publication with a new identity and greater version. The design must define how the invalidation signal travels (control record versus channel teardown) without inventing an `ai.*` method; it must be bounded, ordered, and fail closed.
8. Restart/replacement: helper crash, stdout closure, framing fault, Core shutdown, process kill, digest/version replacement, or new local generation revokes all pending publication, ack, and proof state. Old generation frames/acks are dropped; a replacement helper starts Unbound and must complete handshake + publish + exact ack + equality proof again. No proof survives helper replacement, even if bytes/version are unchanged.

No unbounded buffering or retry loop; restart backoff stays the existing bounded policy.

Unknown control records/versions are rejected without changing lifecycle. A standalone/tolerant helper invocation that never establishes the authenticated publication channel must continue current tolerant behavior; only the future strict provider_list admission is gated. No MCP `list_version` cross-domain compatibility shortcut.

====================================================

2. Exact duplicate/equivalent check
====================================

No equivalent Core implementation was found. #2127 supplies resident digest-verified stdio spawn, bounded framing, and local restart fencing. #2184 supplies generic snapshot-version injection and local acknowledgement. Neither supplies authenticated Core-origin publication ingress, publication-source mapping, remote ack processing, helper proof transport, or proof invalidation across replacement. AI-0324 supplies helper-side canonical parsing/projection plus digest-based lifecycle binding; it does not supply retained-byte exact binding. AI-0327 remains pending acceptance.

The IPC method-registry divergence is not a duplicate or contradiction: Core consumes `aa7259d`, where generic IPC has no `ai.*`; the endpoint consumes `f201911`, where CTX-0006 added the 13 `ai.*` methods. Registration of those methods still does not create publication-control ingress or authentication.

3. A/B candidates — recommendation only, no mechanism ruling
===============================================================

### A — Launch-bound stdio/control channel

Candidate smallest change: retain the Core-created resident stdio pair and add an explicitly designed, bounded, versioned control handshake/record path, either on the framed stream or a separately inherited control fd/handle if control/data multiplexing is rejected. Core would correlate records with its private pending publication and local helper generation; helper would accept only the current channel and issue lifecycle responses. This is not accepted.

Risks that remain unresolved: anonymous inherited stdio does not expose `SO_PEERCRED`; a same-user process obtaining or inheriting an fd/handle could be indistinguishable without another accepted authority mechanism; inherited fd/handle leakage, launch-token/handshake design, Windows handle semantics, channel confusion, replay, generation replacement, and proof revocation remain open. Digest-verified spawn and private normal inheritance are evidence of launch provenance, not sufficient authority by themselves.

### B — OS-attested local control endpoint

Candidate alternative: use a Unix-domain socket / Windows named-pipe control endpoint with bounded records, endpoint/ACL checks, peer credential checks where supported, and channel/generation binding. This is not accepted and must not be described as automatically authenticating Core.

At the consumed Core pin, `VerifiedPeer` proves UID equality (and the Windows SID equality helper is test-only); it does not distinguish an authorized Core component/instance from another same-user process. Endpoint ownership/ACL, peer UID/SID, client-echoed channel IDs, and local generation values alone are insufficient. B therefore still requires an independently accepted Core-component authorization mechanism and must address Linux, BSD-family, Windows, endpoint replacement, inherited fd/handle leakage, and generation/channel gaps.

### Review recommendation

Compare A and B as candidates. Select neither in this dossier. The eventual design must demonstrate authorized Core component identity and binding to the live component/channel/session, not merely same-user or endpoint identity. If either candidate cannot meet that requirement on Linux/BSD/Windows, it must be rejected or revised by the design/security review. No mechanism ruling and no implementation scope is granted here.

4. Bounded lifecycle and transport requirements
===============================================

These are requirements for the future accepted design, not implemented facts:

1. Establish a versioned control protocol and an authority-bearing Core/helper channel handshake. Missing, malformed, unknown-version, timeout, wrong-channel, or insufficient-authority handshakes fail closed before publication acknowledgement or proof.
2. Define how authorized Core component identity is established for both A and B. Explicitly cover Linux, BSD-family platforms, Windows, anonymous/inherited stdio, inherited fd/handle leakage, process replacement, endpoint replacement, and local generation confusion. UID/SID/ACL equality alone is not sufficient.
3. Core derives the exact credential-free provider-routing publication from an accepted source, mints a never-reused publication identity and increasing Core version, and publishes only on the authorized current channel. Core does not become provider client, credential holder, selector, I/O owner, or registry authority.
4. Helper validates bounded domain/identity/version/projection/digest input and returns an ack tied to the current authorized channel. Caller-supplied identity/version/digest/metadata echoes never establish origin or authority.
5. Core accepts an ack only if it matches the current pending identity/domain/version/digest and the live authorized helper generation/channel/session. Any mismatch, stale/future/replay/duplicate/superseded/wrong-channel ack leaves the state Unbound.
6. Helper performs the future accepted AI-0327 retained-byte/byte-for-byte bind/current checks, in addition to the current canonical parsing/projection and digest lifecycle. Strict `ai.provider_list` remains disabled until that accepted helper proof is current.
7. Existing 13 `ai.*` request schemas remain unchanged unless a separate accepted wire decision changes them. No `ai.publish`, `ai.ack`, or invalidation method is guessed here. Generic `snapshot_version` and MCP `list_version` are not provider-routing authority.
8. Provider/model/capability/context/cost mutation and alias-table mutation invalidate helper proof before handler contact. Core source mutation invalidates its pending/ack state and requires a new publication identity/version. The accepted design must define whether invalidation is a bounded control record or channel teardown without inventing an AI method.
9. Crash, stdout closure, framing fault, shutdown, process kill, digest/version replacement, endpoint replacement, generation change, authorization loss, or timeout revokes pending publication, ack, and proof state. A replacement helper starts Unbound even if bytes/version are unchanged.
10. Bounds, queue behavior, deadlines, ordering, no-contact refusal behavior, and protocol compatibility must be explicit. Unknown control records/versions fail closed. Standalone/tolerant operation remains available without publication; strict provider-list admission is the only later gate in this scope.

5. Registry projection and source mapping
=========================================

- The helper remains authoritative for the populated `ProviderRegistry` consumed by `ai.provider_list`. Current AI-0324 maps provider ID, model name, closed capability labels, context-window value, and input/output cost weights into canonical projection bytes/digest, with deterministic ordering and aliases excluded initially. It is currently a canonical parsing/projection + digest-based binding seam, not retained-byte exact binding.
- AI-0327's pending accepted outcome is bounded publication-byte retention and byte-for-byte bind/current checking. Its review/merge and consumed pin must precede strict downstream wiring. Do not represent its isolated implementation as accepted or complete.
- Core's current `ServiceMetadata`/`AiMetadataProducer` is not the provider-routing source: it carries service/version/capability strings, has a 16 KiB generic snapshot bound, and deliberately defers provider/model/routing facts. It cannot be relabeled as the canonical provider-routing projection.
- A future docs decision must map the exact credential-free source of Core publication bytes while preserving helper registry authority. Candidate source mappings remain: (a) a shared registration/install metadata source independently feeding Core's read-only publication view and helper registry, or (b) a helper-to-Core read-only projection feed used as input to Core-owned publication identity/version while helper equality remains independently authoritative. Neither mapping is accepted or implemented.
- `bitty-ipc` DTO/canonicalizer placement remains unresolved. A shared DTO/canonicalizer should be considered only after an accepted transport design proves both sides must share it; otherwise use one-side canonicalization with reviewed test vectors. No pin bump or dependency change is implied.

6. Design-first sequencing and acceptance gates
================================================

Before AI-0329 strict success:

1. Accept a canonical docs/security decision comparing A/B and defining authorized Core component identity for both, without treating UID/SID/ACL or same-user possession as sufficient by itself.
2. Accept the Core publication-source mapping and helper registry ownership boundary.
3. Accept AI-0327's retained-byte/byte-for-byte implementation and verify its merged revision and consumed pin.
4. Only then scope Core ingress/event-loop integration for the selected design. That task must include platform-specific authority work, fd/handle leakage controls, generation/channel/session binding, invalidation, bounded protocol compatibility, and no-contact tests.
5. Only after those gates may AI-0329 wire strict `ai.provider_list` against helper-issued proof.

Required independent security review must cover: same-user injection, anonymous stdio, inherited fd/handle leakage, Linux peer identity, BSD peer identity, Windows named-pipe/handle identity, endpoint replacement, executable replacement, channel confusion, replay, stale/future/duplicate/superseded identity, generation replacement, timeout/backpressure, malformed/oversized control records, source drift, secret/provider-I/O leakage, and tolerant standalone behavior.

MECHANISM: PublicationState owns Arc<PublicationStateLifetime> {sequence: u64, revoked: AtomicBool}; sequence is minted from a process-local AtomicU64 (Relaxed fetch_update, overflow mints a revoked sentinel and fails closed). The token is copied into ProviderRoutingBinding as a private opaque PublicationLifetimeToken; it is never serialized, accepted from frames/acks/callers, or exposed by accessor/Debug (both state and proof Debug are redacted). Clones share the same Arc cell; reset() performs an irreversible SeqCst revoked.store(true), clears all state, and mints a fresh lifetime for recovery. No pointer/address identity, no caller lifetime input, no transport/clock/fs/thread creation, no new deps. The process-wide counter only distinguishes helper-side in-memory lifetimes; it is not Core authority (documented in code + API.md).

REFUSALS: ProviderRoutingError::PublicationLifetimeRevoked (revoked shared cell) and ProviderRoutingError::PublicationLifetimeMismatch (different active/reconstructed lifetime), checked before tuple/bytes/epoch/revision; provider publish/ack/bind also fail closed on a revoked lifetime. Implement the helper-side half of the launch-scoped mutual-certificate control transport, following the committed draft design in bitty-ai-docs architecture/authenticated-provider-publication.md (CTX-0168 / PR #295) and the AI-0303 fail-closed seam.

Scope (slice 1):
- New helper-side module for bounded launch-manifest ingestion: parse the existing launch manifest field sequence plus the appended launch key-material block (profile, key type, Core cert DER, helper cert DER, helper PKCS#8 key), checked lengths, exact EOF, unknown profile/key-type rejection, no allocation before bounds.
- Validate helper certificate/key consistency, derive the Core leaf SHA-256 DER pin, and build a rustls ServerConfig: TLS 1.3 only, ALPN provider-publication-control/1, custom ClientCertVerifier accepting exactly one end-entity certificate whose SHA-256 DER digest matches the pin, delegating signature checks to the provider helpers, no intermediates/chains, no resumption/tickets/0-RTT.
- Accept the TLS session over an injected Read+Write stream; expose the established peer certificate and handshake completion to the dispatch layer; zeroize owned manifest/key buffers after configuration.
- Tests: manifest parse/reject vectors (truncation, oversize, trailing bytes, unknown profile/key type, wrong lengths), pin mismatch, successful mutual handshake against an in-test rustls client fixture, ALPN mismatch, TLS 1.2 refusal, no key material in Debug/log output.
- No control records/state machine yet (slice 2); strict dispatch remains Unbound; no Core changes; no bitty-ipc contract-module extraction yet.

Out of scope: Core supervisor side, bitty-ipc-api pure contract module, AI-0329 strict enablement, platform handle-inheritance evidence, crypto-provider adoption decision.

Deliverable: scoped branch/worktree, tests, local gates green, PR linked to the issue; independent review before merge.","displayId":"AI-0333","id":"01M5AB8J3N6706RD27NTHZTZ6G","priority":"high","status":"ready","title":"Helper-side mutual-cert control transport: launch manifest ingestion and TLS server"}

{"description":"Priority: P1 | Area: security | Labels: feat, P1, area:security | Milestone: v0.1.0 | RFC: none | Task: AI-0337

Issue: #535

## Context

AI-0333 added the helper-side launch-scoped mutual-certificate TLS transport (`crates/bitty-ai-control`), and AI-0336 pinned `bitty-ipc-api` at `e6a2c0c`, which carries the pure `provider_publication` contract module. This task is the helper-side application state machine over the authenticated control session. Strict `ai.provider_list` remains disabled; no data-channel admission, no provider handler.

## Scope

- Add `bitty-ipc-api` (rev e6a2c0c) to `crates/bitty-ai-control`.
- Bounded framed record I/O over the injected TLS session: u32 big-endian length prefix, 256 KiB frame max, 4 KiB small-record bound, no unbounded buffering, caller-owned deadlines.
- `Establish` validation against launch-manifest expectations (every non-secret field, exact constants), then `Established` with a fresh OS-random lifetime_id.
- Initial `Projection` from an injected registry view (feed revision, canonical provider-routing bytes, digest).
- `Publish -> Ack -> Bind -> Bound`: validate authenticated origin, current lifetime/feed revision, strictly increasing publication version, exact tuple, canonical payload/digest; retain exactly one pending publication; consume the exact ack once; compare retained bytes with the current registry projection under the registry read gate; emit the receipt only on equality.
- Invalidation and lifetime rotation with one retired predecessor window, including Core-origin invalidation (`Lifetime -> Projection`), helper-origin reset/reconstruction, and registry mutation sequences.
- Closed reason/error enums, fixed diagnostics with no echoed payload/IDs/paths/secrets, revoke-on-unknown behavior.
- No listener, socket, thread, or clock; no data-channel reservation or `Admit`; no strict enablement; no provider I/O.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests cover golden establishment/projection vectors, publish/ack/bind/bound ordering, duplicates/out-of-order/cross-lifetime records, mutation between Ack and Bind (Bind refuses), retained-byte equality, predecessor-window rotation, bounds, and fail-closed revocation.
- `just check` passes; independent security review approves the state machine and tests.
- Strict remains disabled; no integrated-authority claim.","displayId":"AI-0337","id":"01M5BCB179Z3EFATA7JWGEGC0T","priority":"high","status":"ready","title":"Helper-side provider-publication establishment state machine"}

## Scope (canonical repo only)

   - For every checkout, including branch `main`, verify `HEAD` is equal to or an ancestor of `origin/main` using the same accepted-ancestry rule as the `snapshot-source` gate.

## Non-goals

- Do not re-vendor the six extension repositories in this task; record that as a follow-up on #543.
- No CarryCtx behavior, no release, no remote push.

{"content":"Architecture P0 review — AI-0347 (`agent/headed-agent-contracts-candidate.md`, bitty-ai-docs head 1243a14; document unchanged since 5d63ffc).

Verdict: **NEEDS-FIX** (High x8, Medium x9, Low x5). P0 Architecture row recommendation: **NEEDS-FIX; do not record approval; keep the row Pending.** The document remains `draft`; no contract family is accepted; AI-0347 stays `in_progress` and is not completed.

Wheel gates not applicable: no Wheel file changed. No files edited, committed, pushed, or PR'd.

## High findings (blocking for the Architecture P0 row)

**H1. Accepted Panel Runtime RFC / Event Bus contract is omitted and misstated.**
Evidence: candidate L145 calls the Event Bus "planned; not implemented here"; L146 calls Panel "planned"; L1288 says Core panel and Event Bus implementation "Would need its own accepted contract before implementation; this draft authorizes none". That is false. `bitty-terminal-docs/specifications/panel-runtime-rfc.md` is `status: accepted` (L7), fixes the panel lifecycle `Declared -> Created -> Mounted -> Focused -> Suspended -> Disposed` and `(PanelId, Generation)` (L141-176), the host-mediated Event Bus topic/payload/queue/ordering/drop rules (L349-432), and PR-1..PR-12 bounds (L520-543). `bitty-docs/docs/decisions/rfcs/***REDACTED***.md` is `status: accepted` (L11) and states the generic Panel Runtime container and Event Bus contract is accepted (L29-30). The candidate's "Affected contracts" row (L1288) must be corrected: contract accepted, implementation partial/experimental, cross-process routing/taxonomy/capability ledger open (Panel Runtime RFC L704-718).
Required: add Panel Runtime RFC + RFC-0006 to Normative sources, Affected contracts, and References; replace "planned"/"would need its own accepted contract"; map attachment states to the accepted panel lifecycle and `(PanelId, Generation)`; state that the accepted `panel.*` capability family is not a topic namespace; cite PR-1..PR-12 and `DropOldest`/`DropNewest`.

**H2. Provider/routing ownership contradicts the accepted R1 binding.**
Evidence: candidate L244 gives `headed.routing` the AI owner alone; L321 says `bitty-ai` owns the routing snapshot; L1143 says "AI owner of resolution and routing snapshot". The accepted R1 section says **Core owns publication authority** (derives/publishes the exact canonical projection, mints the monotonic version, owns invalidation) and **the helper owns the authoritative populated registry/proof**; transport placement is unassigned (`architecture/execution-ownership-r1.md` L418-441). The candidate also says R1 is "Consumed unchanged ... ownership proof" (L1279).
Required: `headed.routing` owners = Core owner (publication/version) + AI owner (registry resolution/proof); split the matrix cells accordingly; do not say AI owns the routing snapshot.

**H3. `CP-5 current_generation` is conflated with the session generation.**
Evidence: candidate L404 says "`current_generation` bound to the session generation under CP-5"; the candidate's own axes table (L396-405) says session generation and context snapshot generation are separate axes. AI architecture CP-5 (L167) binds `current_generation` to **AG-2**, and AG-2 (L199) binds agent levels to `(PluginId, generation)` or `(AgentId, generation)`; the AI runtime already has `AgentSession.generation` starting at 1 and `rotate_generation` (`bitty-ai/crates/bitty-ai-runtime/src/session.rs` L332-341, L455-462).
Required: define the relationship explicitly. Either the session generation **is** the AG-2 agent generation (cite the runtime and CP-5), or it is a separate application-level fence and cannot be CP-5's `current_generation`. Do not assert both.

**H4. The session authority split is both declared open and partially decided.**
Evidence: candidate L318-324 says "whether the durable session record and generation issuance live in Core or `bitty-ai` remain open"; L401 says the exact Core-vs-AI split remains open; but L423 fixes "The Core owner owns the session-generation sequence. One Core-designated sequencer assigns ...". A sequencer cannot fence a generation it did not issue without a stated handoff. The open point (L1328) asks only about durable handle/generation/reconnect and omits **state-machine consumption**. The runtime's own `AgentSession` is `Active/Completed/Failed/Canceled` (session.rs L210-218) with `cancel()` L409-412 and `finish()` L446-452, while the candidate maps `stop` to `Completed`/`Failed` and calls `Unknown` a recorded outcome then collapses it (L367-373). AW-1 also assumes session `Canceled` (AI architecture L208).
Required: either (a) leave sequencing in the open point and state the invariant that the generation issuer and sequencer must be the same authority, with an explicit handoff before the first event, or (b) designate the session authority and record why. Add state-machine consumption to the open point. Add a two-level outcome table: session terminal state vs effect/job outcome (`Succeeded`/`Failed`/`Cancelled`/`Unknown`), preserving `Unknown` as reconciliation, not a terminal success/failure.

**H5. Accepted OQ-058/SMO delivery semantics and ADR-0013 identity/GenerationId are omitted.**
Evidence: `bitty-docs/docs/decisions/open-questions.md` L106 records OQ-058 **accepted** (SMO-1..SMO-4 topology including envelope identity, attribution, deadline, priority, dedup, cancellation, expiry; presentation non-authoritative; implementation bitty#1001). The candidate's normative sources (L84-121) and panel/Event Bus section (L625-692) never cite OQ-058 or SMO-1..SMO-4; the topic rules (L650-670) omit envelope identity, dedup, deadline/priority/expiry. ADR-0013 is accepted and defines `Session` (L64), `Agent` lifecycle in `bitty-ai` (L67), and `GenerationId` fencing for reloads/leases/handoffs (L80); the candidate cites neither ADR-0013 nor OQ-084. The AI architecture SMO section is still marked candidate (L700-719), so relying on it does not consume the accepted OQ.
Required: add OQ-058/SMO-1..SMO-4 and ADR-0013 to Normative sources and References; map topic families to the accepted event kinds/delivery semantics; align session/attachment/panel generations with `GenerationId` and the accepted `(PanelId, Generation)`; flag the AI architecture SMO status lag as a follow-up outside this document.

**H6. The P0 gate set is smaller than the task and the document's own review roles.**
Evidence: the P0 table (L1390-1405) has seven rows: Architecture, Security, Core/bittyd, bitty-ai, Wheel, Plugin ecosystem, Documentation. It omits **Product** and **Accessibility**, although the task's required dispositions name product and accessibility and the document defines them as review roles (L1126-1134) and assigns open points to them (Synthetic speech disclosure L1340 Product; Accessibility baseline L1343 Accessibility). The table calls itself the "single authoritative sign-off set" and says later summaries "do not define a smaller role list" (L1390-1392), but it is smaller than the task's list. This is independently recorded as PX-1551 finding 1.
Required: add Product and Accessibility rows (making nine) or explicitly delegate their dispositions to named rows, update the "seven-row" wording throughout, and reconcile with AI-0347's disposition list before any sign-off.

**H7. Event Bus authority is weaker than the accepted contract.**
Evidence: candidate L471 says control/authority overflow "Refuse the newest request"; Panel Runtime RFC L395-410 fixes `DropOldest` as the v1 default with `DropNewest` as a documented alternative, both counted, silent loss prohibited. The candidate does not cite the accepted default or an explicit exception. Candidate L650-670 reserves only `session.*`, `panel.*`, `tool.approval.*`, `tool.result.*`, and host-service namespaces; `ai.*` is not reserved even though AI owns it. The accepted Event Bus requires `owner.name:topic` grammar and manifest-declared produce/consume with `UndisclosedTopic` (Panel Runtime RFC L357-374, L415-427); the candidate's rules do not adopt them, and its `panel.*` topic family collides with the accepted closed `panel.*` capability family (Panel Runtime RFC L436-438; RFC-0006 `panel.*` mapping).
Required: cite the accepted `DropOldest` default and justify the control-class `DropNewest` exception (or use the accepted policy); adopt the topic grammar, manifest declaration, `UndisclosedTopic`, per-principal ledger; reserve `ai.*` for the AI owner; distinguish topic namespaces from the `panel.*` capability family.

**H8. Speech status set and `Unknown` semantics contradict the multimodal boundary the document claims to reuse.**
Evidence: multimodal boundary L235-252 defines `Queued, Preparing, Running, Streaming, Completed, Failed, Cancelled, Unknown`; terminal states are `Completed`, `Failed`, `Cancelled`; `Unknown` is the reconciliation state (L254-263). Candidate L447-448 lists only `queued, running, completed, cancelled, unknown` as "lifecycle and terminal events"; candidate L791 lists `queued, preparing, running, streaming, terminal`; candidate L847-851 calls `Unknown` a terminal outcome. The document says it "reuses ... the status set" (L776-782), but it does not.
Required: use the exact multimodal status set; mark `Unknown` as reconciliation, not terminal; keep the terminal set `Completed/Failed/Cancelled`; align the flow and terminal-event tables.

## Medium findings

**M1. Contract families overlap.** `headed.context` includes session snapshot references (L245) while `headed.session` `attach` returns a session snapshot (L350); `headed.panels` includes "panel attachment, suspend, resume" (L247) while `headed.session` owns `attach`/`detach` (L242) and Panel Runtime RFC owns panel lifecycle; `headed.stream` (L243) and the Event Bus topic rules (L650-670) both define delivery classes, ordering, retention, and backpressure. Required: name the authoritative family for each shared mechanic and cross-reference, or add a family-boundary table.

**M2. Version negotiation has two "single authority" claims and an unguarded minor downgrade.** L255 says the `start` session generation is the single authority for every family; L274-277 adds a standalone `headed.platform` handshake; L264 allows `attach` to choose a lower minor while L287-290 forbids downgrading a security-relevant semantic. Required: carve out the platform probe explicitly and restrict lower-minor selection to additive, non-security-relevant fields with an attributed decision.

**M3. Audio focus is decided while declared open.** L751-753 fixes "at most one attachment holds audio playback focus at a time"; the open point L1336 asks whether focus is per panel, per session, or global. Required: state the physical per-device exclusivity invariant and leave the scope policy open, or resolve the open point.

**M4. Suspend/resume and hidden/invisible contradictions.** L721 says local attachment handles "and their generations do expire" on suspend, while L726-736 resume reuses the same attachment generation and only a mismatch requires a fresh `attach`; either suspend expires the generation (resume impossible) or it does not. L756 says a panel that becomes invisible "is suspended or detached according to host policy", while L764 says "Panel hidden | Attachment continues Yes" and Panel Runtime RFC L152-153 says suspend is becoming invisible **without destroying attachment**. Required: align with the accepted panel lifecycle; define attachment vs panel suspension explicitly.

**M5. Attribution and inherited caps are narrower than the normative sources.** L487-489 and L977-979 attribute drops/enforcement to session, session generation, attachment generation, topic, and budget dimension; FS-AI4 (AI architecture L1036) requires authenticated client id, `AgentId`, `generation`, `StreamHandle` when applicable, Stable Id set, budget dimension, observed value, limit, and action taken. The document says "inherited RFC caps continue to apply" (L485-486, L982-984) without naming RC-9/RC-10, Panel Runtime PR-1..PR-12, or the Isolation Resource RFC queue bounds. Required: adopt FS-AI4's minimum fields plus the headed additions, and cite the inherited caps by document/section.

**M6. Open-point routing and blocker links need correction.** L1328 routes the session authority split to `OQ-061` as primary; OQ-061 is identity-domain separation and panel projection (bitty-docs open-questions L109), not durable session handle/generation/reconnect, and ADR-0013 already supplies `Session`/`GenerationId` terms. L1330 lists "Wheel owner + Plugin ecosystem owner" for coding-capability access, but the promotion target is Core/`bitty-ai` (L213-216). L1335 assigns 3D renderer placement to plugin ecosystem rather than a media/architecture owner. The `Blocks` column omits `headed.context`, `headed.tools`, and `headed.budget` from the session split, and no open point covers the Event Bus contract dependency (it is accepted, not open, but the document must still cite it). L1322 says the table is "not a local blocker set" while the table has a `Blocks` column. Required: correct the primary routing/owners, complete the affected-family column, add the Event Bus dependency as an accepted-contract prerequisite rather than an open point, and reword the note.

**M7. `bitty-agent-api` precision.** L317-319 says the AI runtime's vocabulary dependency is `bitty-agent-api`, not the state-machine crate; L1140 says it "Uses `bitty-agent-api`". In fact `bitty-agent-api` exposes only `AgentId` and `AgentError` (`bitty-agent/crates/bitty-agent-api/src/lib.rs` L5-6); the runtime defines its own `AgentSession` (`bitty-ai-runtime/src/session.rs` L210-218) and the vocabulary-conformance ledger records the drift from `bitty-agent@a8e4112` (`bitty-ai/crates/bitty-ai-runtime/tests/vocabulary_conformance.rs` L1-18, L487-504). Required: state the exact dependency (IDs/errors only), name the runtime's separate `AgentSession` and its `Canceled` state, and do not imply the accepted state machine is consumed.

**M8. Platform tier terminology and matrix claims.** The document uses presentation tiers A-D (L997-1008) while ADR-0002 uses platform support tiers 1-3 (L52-59); "FreeBSD Tier C or D by default" (L1021) is ambiguous across the two scales. L1013 says "Core's published platform support matrix remains authoritative" without a link; no published matrix was found, while ADR-0002 is the accepted tier source. Required: rename the presentation tiers (or qualify them as presentation tiers), cite ADR-0002 for platform support, and link it.

**M9. Cross-review consistency items that remain open.** The execution-projection binding is called "governing" (L688-692, L749-750) although the linked document is `status: draft` and accepts nothing (also PX-1551 finding 3). `TODO.md` L29-34 still labels the item "AI-0343" and records only the 16 open points, not AI-0347 or the seven P0 rows (also PX-1551 finding 2). The Wheel boundary cites only bitty-ai-docs drafts, not Wheel README/SECURITY-MODEL/repo.toml (PX-1550 P1-1). Required: qualify the binding as candidate, update TODO.md to AI-0347 plus the P0 gate set, and cite Wheel's authoritative sources or explicitly label them as draft.

## Low findings

- L528 lists capabilities "vision" and "speech"; the accepted closed labels are `image_input`/`audio_input`/`audio_output` (R1 L315-318) and the provider boundary uses "vision" only as an illustrative example (L113-116). Map or mark aliases as illustrative.
- L425-430 says a dropped event still consumes a sequence number "so a consumer can distinguish a dropped event from an event that was never produced"; the numbering rule distinguishes committed-then-dropped from never-committed, not two event classes. Reword.
- L1202 says "No implementation exists"; this is true for the headed Agent but not for the cited sibling surfaces (experimental PanelRegistry, in-process EventBus in bundled-disabled consumers, runtime `AgentSession`). Scope the sentence.
- L629-643 uses `session.lifecycle.*`/`ai.turn.*` family labels against the accepted `owner.name:topic` grammar (Panel Runtime RFC L357-360); say explicitly they are pre-wire labels and that eventual names must use the accepted grammar.
- L1322 "not a local blocker set" conflicts with the `Blocks` column; reword to "review index; the Blocks column names affected families for family-level acceptance".

## What passes

- Draft honesty is strong: `status: draft`, "it remains draft", no P0 sign-off, no contract family accepted, no implementation claim, explicit residual risks, and seven pending rows (L14-24, L1388-1405). The document does not authorize implementation.
- The sibling boundary is sound: no Wheel-Headed edge (L188-190), no headed UI/speech/avatar/3D work assigned to Wheel (L201, L219-230, L1157), and the `wheel.*` prohibition is explicit (L206-217). This matches Wheel README Option B (L31-39), subject to PX-1550 P1-1's sourcing correction.
- The security posture is fail-closed and reviewable: presentation-never-authority, default-deny consent, redaction before queue/write, no autoplay, isolated decode, no hidden context, and explicit residual risks (L1041-1214).

- Implementers could follow the candidate's panel/Event Bus vocabulary instead of the accepted Panel Runtime RFC/RFC-0006, eroding the accepted `(PanelId, Generation)` lifecycle, PR bounds, and `DropOldest` behavior.
- The session authority split could duplicate or contradict authority between Core and `bitty-ai` when the future `bittyd` contract lands; the candidate's Core-owned sequencer plus open generation issuance is not implementable as written.

- The P0 gate could be signed without Product and Accessibility dispositions, leaving the speech-disclosure and accessibility baselines unowned.
- Unpromoted follow-up issues could be lost; the 16 open points are an index, not a tracked register.

This note does not review uncommitted text as the candidate; re-review the committed corrected revision when it lands.

Sources read: candidate (1440 lines); accepted ADR 0016 Boundary 3 (bitty-docs `docs/decisions/adrs/***REDACTED***.md` L234-262, L375-378); accepted accessibility extraction contract (bitty-terminal-docs `specifications/accessibility-extraction-contract.md` L16-23, L160-209, L281-351, L353-368, L419-426, L490-503); draft Accessibility Baseline (L79-118, L190-202); accepted RFC-0002 reduced motion (L169-181); accepted RFC-0001 contrast (L277-298); `bitty-a11y` README (L3-7); Panel Runtime RFC focus/overlay (L303-315); plugin docs U-9 (L420-438); OQ-078 (bitty-docs `docs/decisions/open-questions.md` L124); AI architecture rich streaming (L217-222). Workspace search found no existing caption/transcript, media-control, or headed-surface screen-reader contract; OQ-078 remains open.

## PASS (frame is honest; direction is usable)

- Draft honesty: L14-24, L54-66, L1404-1405; no implementation or P0 sign-off claim.
- No-autoplay: playback off by default, explicit revocable user-owned policy or fresh gesture (L869-875). Compatible with accessible media, provided the fresh gesture can be keyboard/AT activation.
- Presentation-never-authority: presentation cannot approve/execute; approval requires an explicit Core action (L615-618, L1189). Compatible, but must be extended to the accessibility projection/action (H7).
- Avatar and motion direction: avatar is presentation, never identity/authority (L881-897); reduced-motion/static/text-only modes are first-class (L903-904); captions/transcript and no-hidden-context statements (L873-874, L942-943, L1093) are the right starting point.
- Media privacy baseline: media extension must not read transcripts, capture camera/mic, or persist media (L204, L946-947). Good, but it creates the caption-owner question in H5.

## High (blocking the Accessibility row)

**H1. The authoritative P0 table has no Accessibility row.**
Evidence: L1126-1134 defines **Accessibility owner** as a review role; L1162-1167 calls the table "seven-row" and "the single authoritative sign-off set"; L1390-1405 lists seven rows and none is Accessibility; L1198 still expects "Seven review records"; L1404 says "all seven rows". AI-0347 explicitly requires an accessibility disposition, and AI-0354 exists for that row; a P0 gate that omits it can be signed without an accessibility decision. The corrections branch intro already says "nine rows", but the table is not updated in the uncommitted draft either.
Required: add an **Accessibility** row (and coordinate the **Product** row with AI-0353), update every "seven-row"/"seven review records" reference, and make the acceptance criteria and independent-review gate count the full set. The row evidence must cite this review and the accepted accessibility contract. Do not mark the row Approved until H2-H7 and M1-M4 close.

**H2. Accepted accessibility contracts are omitted and accepted obligations are reopened as an open point.**
Evidence: the normative-sources list (L84-121) and affected-contracts table (L1276-1290) cite no accessibility document. L944-945 says "Flashing, rapid motion, and high-contrast effects follow the host's accessibility settings and can be disabled." L1343 asks "Which reduced-motion, caption, contrast, and screen-reader behaviors are mandatory versus optional?" That reopens requirements that are already accepted at the boundary: ADR 0016 Boundary 3 (L243-254) retains the accessibility baseline, focus-order rule, bounded announcements, reduced-motion and contrast respect, and the projection-never-authority/privacy rule; the accepted W-134 extraction contract (L162-167, L389-391) fixes the retained Core mechanism and says reduced motion collapses to the final committed state and high contrast selects the compliant theme pair, neither plugin-overridable. RFC-0002 (L173-181) fixes accepted reduced-motion semantics; RFC-0001 (L277-298) fixes accepted non-text contrast rules. OQ-078 (L124) remains open only on the API/tree choice, ownership relative to the Scene model/platform adapters, and v1 scope; the accepted boundary and retained baseline are not open.
Required: add ADR 0016 Boundary 3 and the W-134 accessibility extraction contract to Normative sources, Affected contracts, and References. Add the draft Accessibility Baseline, theme-token contract, and UI-motion candidate as draft inputs that are consumed but not promoted. State that every headed surface inherits the Core accessibility baseline unchanged and may not weaken it. Split the open point: (a) accepted obligations are not open; (b) genuinely media-specific decisions (caption presentation, transcript retention, avatar alternative content, media-control semantics, caption contrast floor) get named owners and tracked register/task routing. Replace "can be disabled" with "must be honored and is not plugin-overridable" for high contrast, and treat flashing/rapid motion separately.

**H3. Headed surface screen-reader semantics, focus behavior, and keyboard access are unowned.**
Evidence: L679 says Core owns "host focus and visibility rules" and the Headed Agent owns "internal composition and widgets"; no requirement makes those widgets semantically exposed. L202 assigns "chat and interaction composition, presentation policy" to the plugin. There is no role/name/state mapping for the chat transcript, streaming messages, tool approvals, speech controls, captions, or avatar; no focus order, no announcements, no modal focus confinement, no focus restoration, and no keyboard-equivalence rule. The accepted extraction contract requires scene/terminal/chrome mapping and interactive role/name/state (L190-209), Core-owned focus association and order, modal confinement (L281-300), and a controlled action interface (L323-351). AI architecture RS-4 requires streamed rich fragments to remain accessible after composition (L217-222); the candidate claims rich streaming reuse but never binds that guarantee. Plugin U-9 candidate guidance requires standard components to bind roles, names, keyboard activation, focus, disabled/busy states, and announcements (L420-438), but is not cited.
Required: add a top-level headed-accessibility subsection that requires every headed UI element presented through Core scene/panel primitives to carry an accessible role, name, state, and activation, and to fail closed or omit the element when no mapping exists. Define: chat/transcript order and message roles; code/diff/tool-card semantics; streaming announcements on transitions (never per token); approval request announcement without focus theft; modal focus confinement and restoration; Core-owned focus with no plugin focus stealing; visible focus; keyboard equivalents for every pointer action; and the rule that semantics is derived, read-only, never authority, never persisted, and never published on the Event Bus. Reuse the standard component semantics rather than inventing a second accessibility tree. Add conformance tests for role/name/state, focus order, modal focus, keyboard equivalence, and announcement coalescing.

**H4. Platform accessibility exposure is absent from `headed.platform` and the presentation tiers.**
Evidence: the platform layer detects capabilities and defines tiers A-D (L996-1004), but its capability list and rules cover audio/GPU/decoder only (L1026-1034). There is no AT-SPI/D-Bus, Windows UI Automation, or macOS AX owner, no accessibility capability or platform-permission state, no behavior when the adapter is absent or denied, and no tier constraint on screen-reader exposure. The accepted extraction contract makes platform exposure a Core-granted, platform-permission-gated capability, and says an absent/denied/crashed adapter removes exposure only (L419-426); it also records that no AT backend exists yet and only `HeadlessBackend` ships (L490-503). `bitty-a11y` README (L7) confirms "no assistive technology sees a Bitty tree yet." Tier C/D therefore cannot be described as accessible merely because they are text-first.
Required: add accessibility exposure to `headed.platform`: Core/`bitty-a11y` owns the adapter and AT bridges; the Headed Agent and media extensions supply semantics only through the Core projection and never call a platform accessibility API directly; no private first-party path. Add an explicit accessibility status (available / unavailable / platform-permission-denied) separate from presentation tiers; an absent or denied adapter must remove exposure only and never fail the session, and no tier may claim screen-reader access without adapter evidence. Record the missing AT backends as a residual risk and add platform tests for absent, denied, and crashed adapters, including safe mode.

**H5. Captions/transcripts are named but not contract-grade, and caption ownership conflicts with the media-extension prohibition.**
Evidence: L942-943 says "Captions **or** a text transcript accompany speech"; L873-874 says they "remain available whenever speech is available"; L839 and L920 say captions continue/remain accurate when visemes are lost; L1093 says the text that produced speech is inspectable. But there is no definition of synchronized captions during playback versus a post-hoc transcript, no caption text source/redaction parity, no locale, timing tolerance, length bound, screen-reader exposure, user toggle, or retention rule, and no verification test. Ownership is unresolved: the media extension must not read transcripts (L204), while the Headed Agent owns "user controls" (L865-867) and `headed.speech` names only the AI owner (contract) and media extension owner (playback) (L248). The workspace has no other caption/transcript contract.
Required: define synchronized captions as mandatory whenever speech is presented, plus an inspectable transcript within the retention window; use "and", not "or". Captions and transcript must be rendered from the same redacted text that was synthesized, contain no hidden context, and create no new persistence class (R3 applies). Assign caption/transcript presentation to the Headed Agent owner (or a Core caption primitive); the media extension receives audio/playback data only and never the transcript. Define keyboard/AT-operable caption and transcript controls, contrast/size/position requirements, and non-speech audio cues (errors/alerts) with a visual or text equivalent. Add tests for caption presence and synchronization, text parity, viseme/audio loss, no-audio-device fallback, AT access, and retention/deletion.

**H6. Avatar alternative content and state equivalence are undefined.**
Evidence: the avatar state vocabulary (L883-897) and animation rules (L900-909) define `thinking`, `speaking`, `waiting`, `error`, `suspended`, and `detached`, but the only accessibility text is L946-947, which says the avatar does not read the transcript or capture input. Nothing says whether the avatar is decorative or informative to assistive technology, whether it has an accessible name/description, or how a screen-reader user learns that the agent is thinking, waiting for approval, or has failed. The accepted baseline requires scene nodes to map to roles/names and async state to announce once per transition (L84-89, L103-105); an avatar that carries state without a text equivalent fails that rule.
Required: state that the avatar is decorative and excluded from the accessibility tree by default; if it conveys state, expose an image/graphic role with an accessible name and description **and** present the same state as text in a status region. Announce each semantic state transition once, coalesced, and never convey required information only through animation, expression, color, or viseme. Apply reduced motion/static mode to all avatar transitions; forbid flashing/rapid motion above a safe threshold independent of user settings and avatar-asset content. Add tests for state-text parity, announcement, decorative exclusion, reduced motion, and flash safety.

**H7. Accessibility projection and AT actions are not covered by presentation-never-authority.**
Evidence: the presentation-never-authority gate (L1189) names "a panel, attachment, avatar state, animation, or speech control" but not the accessibility projection or platform adapter; the threat table (L1173) likewise names panel/avatar/attachment. L615-618 correctly requires approval through the Core authorization path, and L1054-1073 correctly denies authority to voice/avatar/model output, but the accessibility adapter is not named. The accepted extraction contract requires the projection to never be authority and AT actions to resolve through Core's controlled action interface and command registry, with no direct terminal mutation and no Event-Bus publication (L323-368).
Required: extend presentation-never-authority, the threat table, and the accessibility gate to the projection and platform adapter. An AT activation of an approval or media control is a presentation action routed through Core's controlled action interface and command registry; it is not a grant, not a separate approval path, and never bypasses consent. The adapter is not a principal; it has no direct terminal mutation and no Event-Bus publication. Add adversarial tests: AT activation without a grant fails closed; AT cannot approve a tool call; forged/stale element handles fail; no projection or focus association leaks onto the bus.

## Medium (needed before the row can sign)

**M1. Accessible media controls are not specified.**
Evidence: L134, L202, and L867 assign "speech controls"/"user controls" to the Headed Agent but define no controls, labels, keyboard behavior, or states. No existing workspace contract covers media controls. The no-autoplay rule (L869-875) implies a play control must exist, but does not make it accessible.
Required: define the media-control surface: play/pause, stop/cancel, replay, mute/volume, playback rate, caption/transcript toggle, and any voice/locale selector offered. Every control must be keyboard and AT operable, labeled with role/name/state, announce its state, and keep stop/cancel reachable at all times. A fresh user gesture may be keyboard/AT activation. Add keyboard-only and screen-reader-only tests.

**M2. Contrast and flashing wording is too weak and partly wrong.**
Evidence: L944-945 treats "high-contrast effects" as something that "can be disabled" and does not state a contrast floor. High contrast is a user accessibility mode to honor, not an optional effect; the accepted RFC-0001 AC-1..AC-3 rules and the theme-token contract define the contrast obligations, and OQ-037 still owns the minimum content contrast. No flashing threshold is defined, and avatar/media assets are untrusted (L1098-1111), so a user setting alone cannot be the only guard.
Required: state that headed surfaces consume Core theme tokens and high-contrast mode, use no hardcoded colors, and meet the accepted text/non-text contrast floors for text, captions, transcripts, controls, focus indicators, and avatar overlays. Route the exact content-contrast floor to the theme-token contract/OQ-037 rather than inventing a value here. Define a flashing/rapid-motion threshold independent of user settings, forbid avatar/media assets from overriding it, and require reduced motion to collapse to the final committed state.

**M3. Verification and acceptance criteria contain no accessibility evidence.**
Evidence: the verification plan (L1216-1250) mentions "reduced motion" only inside avatar/viseme tests (L1243-1244); there are no screen-reader, focus, caption, contrast, keyboard-control, or AT-action tests. The acceptance criteria (L1352-1383) do not mention accessibility, and the security gates (L1185-1198) have no accessibility row.
Required: add an accessibility verification block covering semantics role/name/state, focus order/modal/restoration, announcement coalescing, captions/transcript, keyboard/AT media controls, avatar alternative content, contrast, reduced motion/flash safety, absent/denied adapter degradation, AT action authorization, and no Event-Bus leak. Add accessibility to the acceptance criteria and to the definition of done for each headed contract family.

**M4. The Accessibility open point has no accountable owner or tracked destination, and it blocks the wrong families.**
Evidence: L1343 routes "Accessibility baseline" to "Plugin ecosystem owner + Accessibility owner" with "Follow-up issue"; no accessibility owner appears in any contract family or ownership-matrix row. It blocks only `headed.avatar` and `headed.speech`, while screen-reader/focus/keyboard requirements also affect heading panels, tools/approvals, and the platform family. AI-0347 requires follow-up issues to be promoted into their owning register or scoped issue before sign-off, and the document itself says the open-point table is an index, not a register.
Required: split the open point into accepted obligations (not open) and new media-specific decisions; assign each remaining item an accountable owner and a named register entry or scoped task (not a generic "Follow-up issue"); include `headed.panels`, `headed.tools`, and `headed.platform` in the affected families; state which items are v0.1 blockers and which are deferred.

## Low (track or fix opportunistically)

- **L1. Terminology/section placement.** "Accessibility and privacy" appears only under Avatar (L940), which makes the whole headed surface's accessibility obligations look avatar-specific. Move the Core-baseline obligations to a top-level section and distinguish "Core accessibility baseline (ADR 0016/W-134)" from "media accessibility obligations" so "accessibility baseline" is not confused with the draft candidate document.
- **L2. Caption detail.** Locale/script/direction, timing tolerance, maximum caption length, non-speech cues, and transcript export/retention are not defined. Define them in the caption contract or route them explicitly; do not leave them implicit in "captions remain available".
- **L3. FreeBSD/platform wording.** A text-only tier is not automatically screen-reader accessible, and no AT bridge exists on FreeBSD today. State that platform accessibility exposure is unsupported/unavailable there, rather than implying Tier C/D provides accessibility.

## Required decisions before the Accessibility row can approve

1. Add the Accessibility P0 row (and the Product row, coordinated with AI-0353), update the seven-row wording, and make the independent-review gate count the full set.
2. Cite ADR 0016 Boundary 3 and the accepted W-134 accessibility extraction contract as normative sources, affected contracts, and references; state that the headed design consumes the Core baseline and weakens none of it.
3. Define headed screen-reader semantics, focus order, announcements, keyboard equivalence, and modal focus behavior as a contract requirement over Core's projection, not an open question.
4. Define platform accessibility ownership (Core/`bitty-a11y`), capability/permission gating, absent/denied adapter behavior, and the honest current status that no AT backend ships yet.
5. Define synchronized captions and an inspectable transcript, with the Headed Agent as presentation owner, the media extension kept transcript-free, the same redacted text, and R3 retention.
6. Define avatar alternative content and state equivalence so no required information is conveyed only by the avatar or animation.
7. Define accessible media controls (labels, roles, states, keyboard/AT operation, stop/replay, captions/transcript) and preserve no-autoplay.
8. Extend presentation-never-authority to the accessibility projection and AT actions; no AT action may grant, approve, or bypass Core authorization, and the projection never reaches the Event Bus.
9. Split and promote the accessibility open point into accepted obligations plus named, tracked media-specific decisions, and add accessibility verification/acceptance criteria.

## Residual risks if approved without these fixes

- A headed surface could ship pointer-only or with no screen-reader semantics while the P0 table appears complete, because accessibility is not a gate row.
- Captions could be optional, transcript-only, or unowned; the media extension/transcript prohibition could either block captioning or force transcript access into the wrong component.
- AT activation of an approval or media control could be misclassified as a separate authority path, or blocked entirely, despite the presentation-never-authority rule.
- The platform matrix could imply screen-reader access on tiers where no AT bridge exists; `bitty-a11y` currently exposes no tree to assistive technology.
- The open point could be used to downgrade accepted reduced-motion/contrast obligations to optional behavior.

P0-row recommendation: **NEEDS-FIX; keep the Accessibility row Pending.** Re-review the committed corrected candidate (and the corrected P0 table) before recording any approval. AI-0347 stays `in_progress`; AI-0354 is not completed by this note.
