{"content":"Product P0 disposition — AI-0353 (parent AI-0347)

Verdict: NEEDS-FIX

Scope and revision

- Reviewed bitty-ai-docs main @ 1243a14, the current candidate: agent/headed-agent-contracts-candidate.md.
- The ai-0347/docs-p0-corrections worktree exists at 1243a14 with uncommitted edits to the same file (454 insertions / 214 deletions). I read that worktree read-only; the same seven-row sign-off, the same 16 open points, and no product-scope section remain there. This note is therefore a review of the current main candidate, not of the corrected candidate; re-review is required after the corrections branch/PR lands.
- Read-only review. No files edited, no commit, no PR. AI-0353 and AI-0347 are not marked complete.

What the candidate gets right

- Synthetic-speech disclosure is not claimed as solved: it is listed as a residual risk and as an open point that blocks headed.speech (candidate L1207-1208, L1340). That is honest.
- Product-safety posture is explicit: voice cloning, speaker identification, biometric voiceprints, persistent voice profiles, camera/microphone capture, and face/voice recognition are out of scope (L818-820, L946-947); playback is off by default (L869-875); captions/transcript accompany speech and audio is never the only channel (L942-943); no hidden context in speech (L1093-1094); no model/agent/plugin/avatar gesture can grant approval or start audio (L615-618, L1067-1073).
- Wheel boundary is clear and consistent with the Wheel candidate: no wheel.* dependency, no Wheel plugin slot, no shared UI ownership (L206-230); Wheel's candidate boundary does permit UI plugins including chat (bitty-ai-docs/specifications/wheel-core-plugin-boundary-candidate.md:194-198), so the sibling framing is meaningful.
- No draft-status/implementation-claim conflict found on the Product row. The status block (L14-24), non-claims (L54-66), "No implementation exists" (L1202), and verification statement (L1218-1220) are disciplined. The bitty-agent/bitty-agent-api claim is accurate: bitty/Cargo.toml has no bitty-agent dependency, and bitty-ai/crates/bitty-ai-runtime/Cargo.toml:22 depends on bitty-agent-api at rev a8e4112.

P1 findings

P1-1 — The "single authoritative" P0 gate has no Product or Accessibility row.
Evidence: L1127-1129 defines Product owner and Accessibility owner as review roles; L1340 assigns synthetic speech disclosure to "Security owner + Product owner"; L1343 assigns the accessibility baseline to "Plugin ecosystem owner + Accessibility owner"; L1390 calls the table the "single authoritative sign-off set"; L1394-1402 rows are Architecture, Security, Core/bittyd, bitty-ai, Wheel, Plugin ecosystem, Documentation; L1198 says "Seven review records". AI-0347's own required disposition list names product and accessibility owners.
Impact: the two decisions this document assigns to Product and Accessibility have no sign-off row, so the gate cannot be satisfied as written and this Product disposition has nowhere to land. The "seven-row" claim is also internally inconsistent with the two review roles the document defines.
Required fix: add Product and Accessibility rows (and reviewers) to the sign-off table, update every "seven" reference (L22-24, L1165, L1198, L1390, L1404) and the AI-0347 count, or state explicitly that these roles are subsumed and record where their dispositions live.

P1-2 — No product thesis or v1 scope; the surface is not demonstrably distinct from Wheel's chat UI or the terminal's agent pane.
Evidence: the Purpose defines only reusable contracts for "a future sibling Headed Agent plugin" and says "Headed describes presentation and human interaction" (L28-32); the non-claims remove "Any UI layout, chat transcript design, character design, voice persona, or plugin packaging decision" (L63-64); the only positive product description is "chat and interaction composition, presentation policy, speech controls, and avatar appearance mapping" (L134). Wheel's candidate explicitly permits chat UI plugins (wheel-core-plugin-boundary-candidate.md:194-198), and the candidate leaves "Shared chat or transcript contract" open (L1342). The v0.1 profile has no UI, speech, or network path (product/implementation-profile-v0.1.md:16-46), and the product tree has no admission route for a headed product scope (product/README.md:19-22). The accepted product constraint "agent-friendly, not agent-centric" (bitty-terminal-docs/product/vision.md:152-164) is not cited.
Impact: a Product reviewer cannot say who the product is for, what problem it solves, or whether voice/avatar are in v1. The acceptance criteria (L1358-1386) contain no product-scope criterion, so a draft could pass without one.
Required decision: add a short product-scope section or an explicit open point covering target user, problem, minimum v1 surface (text chat only? speech? avatar?), target milestone, and the relationship to Wheel's chat UI and the terminal's agent panes. Cite the product vision.

P1-3 — Placement is not reconciled with the accepted AI-surface record and assumes an unbuilt Native UI runtime.
Evidence: bitty-terminal-docs/specifications/ai-surface-accepted-record.md:29-33 records that the bitty-terminal.ai-panel entry and its Core module were removed and that "AI surfaces move to the separate optional bitty-ai extension", with A-1..A-7 applying to "any future AI panel built on the generic primitives"; bitty-docs/docs/decisions/index.md:313 repeats the placement. The candidate instead calls the owner "the future sibling plugin repository" (L1121), calls the artifact a plugin throughout (L134, L202, L643), and leaves packaging as Lua plugin / out-of-process component / composed distribution open (L1329). It cites neither the accepted record nor bitty-terminal-docs/specifications/panel-surface-process-trichotomy-candidate.md:189-201, which records that the Native UI framework, surface type system, and process abstraction are "NOT built".
Impact: the product's ownership placement (optional bitty-ai extension vs separate sibling repository vs composed distribution) is assumed rather than decided, and its UI substrate is unbuilt and unsequenced. This is a product-identity question, not only packaging.
Required decision: state and reconcile the placement with the accepted AI-surface record; if the answer is the optional bitty-ai extension, say so; if a separate sibling repository is intended, record that as a new product decision and explain why the accepted placement does not cover it.

P1-4 — Accessibility commitments in the body contradict the open accessibility baseline.
Evidence: L903-904 says reduced-motion, static, and text-only modes are "first-class"; L942-943 says "Captions or a text transcript accompany speech; audio is never the only channel for required information"; L944-945 says flashing/motion/high-contrast follow host settings. L1343 then asks "Which reduced-motion, caption, contrast, and screen-reader behaviors are mandatory versus optional?" and marks headed.avatar and headed.speech blocked. No screen-reader behavior is stated in the body.
Impact: the body reads as settled user-facing commitments while the gate says the same behaviors are undecided; the accessibility reviewer cannot tell what is a floor and what is an aspiration.
Required fix/decision: either state the mandatory floor in the body and let the open point cover only the remainder, or downgrade the body statements to candidate requirements with a pointer; add the screen-reader behavior to the decision; route the result to AI-0354 and add the Accessibility sign-off row (P1-1).

P1-5 — Recording, export, and deletion rights are simultaneously asserted and left open; Tier C's "later playback" has no retention class.
Evidence: L1050-1051 defines a "Recording and retention" consent category defaulting to Off and says "apply deletion under R3"; L1085-1087 says media is "ephemeral by default" and "Recording requires explicit retention consent"; L821-824 requires derived audio/viseme deletion propagation and calls partial propagation "non-conformance"; L1003 promises Tier C "speech may produce an asset for later playback"; L1195 lists "export-preview" tests in the security gate. L1341 then asks "Can users record, export, or delete synthesized audio and viseme data, and under which retention class?".
Impact: user-facing data rights are both promised and undecided. Tier C's later playback presumes retention that the document does not define, and the export-preview gate presumes an export surface whose product scope is open.
Required decision: decide whether record/export is in v1; if yes, name the retention class, export format/preview, and deletion-propagation UX; separate the already-required deletion propagation from the open product capability; align Tier C and the export-preview gate with the decision.

P2 findings

P2-1 — Consent UX is specified as policy but not as a user surface, and is untracked.
Evidence: L1045-1052 defines the consent categories and defaults; L1054-1073 requires per-principal, per-session-generation, per-provider/privacy-class, per-scope, time-bound, "visible", and "revocable" consent, forbids wildcard/allow-all, and requires a fresh prompt after revocation; L1069 requires "an explicit user action through the Core authorization path". The Core authorization path is itself owner-pending (L1288, L1398), and no open point covers the consent prompt or revocation surface.
Impact: the central consent interaction of a voice/chat product has no product requirement. Per-session/per-provider/per-class grants create consent-fatigue and revocation-discoverability risks that no reviewer owns.
Required decision: add an open point or product requirement for prompt placement/content, grant review and revocation, how speech egress is distinguished from model egress, and the consent-fatigue stance.

P2-2 — "Plugin" identity and the "Headed" name are assumed while identity and packaging are open.
Evidence: L134 calls it the "Headed Agent plugin ... Working name only"; L643 uses a plugin.<headed-agent-id> topic family; L1121 calls the owner a "future sibling plugin repository"; L1329 then asks whether it is a Lua plugin, an out-of-process component, or a composed distribution, and who signs/updates it. L1330 and L1342 leave coding capability access and the shared chat contract open. "Headed" describes a trait shared by the terminal and Wheel's TUI; it does not distinguish the product.
Impact: the document commits to plugin/repository identity before that is decided, and the working name does not tell a user what the product is for.
Required decision: mark plugin/repository identity provisional everywhere or decide it; choose a user-facing name/value statement and route naming to product.

P2-3 — Synthetic-speech disclosure is honest but ungated and lacks a product minimum.
Evidence: L1207-1208 says voice provenance, watermarking, and synthetic-speech disclosure "are not defined; a future speech contract must decide them"; L1340 makes it an open point owned by "Security owner + Product owner" and blocks headed.speech; product/ai-unresolved-questions.md:40 says "truthful disclosure ... remain mandatory". Captions (L942-943) disclose content but not that the voice is synthetic, especially in audio-only or autoplay use.
Impact: headed.speech can be accepted without a disclosure minimum, and the Product owner required to decide it has no sign-off row (P1-1).
Required decision: define the minimum disclosure (visible label at playback, spoken disclosure, provenance metadata on exported assets) and its audio-only behavior; keep headed.speech blocked until decided. Do not change the draft status; the current honesty is correct.

Required product decisions (for the Product row)
D1. Product thesis and v1 scope: target user, problem, minimum surface (text chat only? speech? avatar?), target milestone, and relationship to Wheel's chat UI and the terminal's agent panes.
D2. Synthetic-speech disclosure minimum, including audio-only/autoplay behavior and provenance metadata on exported assets.
D3. Record/export/deletion product rights and retention class; align Tier C and the export-preview gate.
D4. Accessibility floor (captions, reduced motion, contrast, screen reader) and what is v1 vs aspiration; align with AI-0354.
D5. Product placement and identity: optional bitty-ai extension vs separate sibling plugin repository vs composed distribution; user-facing name; plugin/repo assumptions.
D6. Consent surface: prompt placement/content, grant review/revocation, speech-vs-model egress distinction, consent-fatigue stance.
D7. Gate correction: add Product and Accessibility sign-off rows and update the counts.

Not a finding

- No Product-row conflict with the draft/no-implementation-claim requirement. The candidate repeatedly disclaims implementation and does not claim the plugin ships or is installable. The implementation claims it does make (bitty-agent state-machine crate not linked by Core; bitty-agent-api as the AI vocabulary dependency; Wheel's candidate UI-plugin permission) are accurate.

Re-review trigger

- Re-review the Product row after the ai-0347/docs-p0-corrections branch/PR lands. {"after":{"content":"Accessibility P0 review — AI-0347 (`agent/headed-agent-contracts-candidate.md`, bitty-ai-docs main head 1243a14; candidate sha256 ***REDACTED***; document unchanged since 5d63ffc).

Verdict: **NEEDS-FIX** (High x7, Medium x4, Low x3). P0 Accessibility row recommendation: **NEEDS-FIX; do not record approval; keep the row Pending.** The document remains `draft`; no contract family is accepted; AI-0347 and AI-0354 are not completed.

Review target: current main candidate, as instructed while `ai-0347/docs-p0-corrections` is in progress. The corrections worktree `.worktrees/ai-0347-docs-p0-corrections` has uncommitted edits (449 insertions/213 deletions): its draft intro already says "nine rows", but the P0 table still has seven rows and the Accessibility section/open point are unchanged. This note does not review uncommitted text as the candidate; re-review the committed corrected revision when it lands.

Sources read: candidate (1440 lines); accepted ADR 0016 Boundary 3 (bitty-docs `docs/decisions/adrs/***REDACTED***.md` L234-262, L375-378); accepted accessibility extraction contract (bitty-terminal-docs `specifications/accessibility-extraction-contract.md` L16-23, L160-209, L281-351, L353-368, L419-426, L490-503); draft Accessibility Baseline (L79-118, L190-202); accepted RFC-0002 reduced motion (L169-181); accepted RFC-0001 contrast (L277-298); `bitty-a11y` README (L3-7); Panel Runtime RFC focus/overlay (L303-315); plugin docs U-9 (L420-438); OQ-078 (bitty-docs `docs/decisions/open-questions.md` L124); AI architecture rich streaming (L217-222). Workspace search found no existing caption/transcript, media-control, or headed-surface screen-reader contract; OQ-078 remains open.

## PASS (frame is honest; direction is usable)

- Draft honesty: L14-24, L54-66, L1404-1405; no implementation or P0 sign-off claim.
- No-autoplay: playback off by default, explicit revocable user-owned policy or fresh gesture (L869-875). Compatible with accessible media, provided the fresh gesture can be keyboard/AT activation.
- Presentation-never-authority: presentation cannot approve/execute; approval requires an explicit Core action (L615-618, L1189). Compatible, but must be extended to the accessibility projection/action (H7).
- Avatar and motion direction: avatar is presentation, never identity/authority (L881-897); reduced-motion/static/text-only modes are first-class (L903-904); captions/transcript and no-hidden-context statements (L873-874, L942-943, L1093) are the right starting point.
- Media privacy baseline: media extension must not read transcripts, capture camera/mic, or persist media (L204, L946-947). Good, but it creates the caption-owner question in H5.

## High (blocking the Accessibility row)

**H1. The authoritative P0 table has no Accessibility row.**
Evidence: L1126-1134 defines **Accessibility owner** as a review role; L1162-1167 calls the table "seven-row" and "the single authoritative sign-off set"; L1390-1405 lists seven rows and none is Accessibility; L1198 still expects "Seven review records"; L1404 says "all seven rows". AI-0347 explicitly requires an accessibility disposition, and AI-0354 exists for that row; a P0 gate that omits it can be signed without an accessibility decision. The corrections branch intro already says "nine rows", but the table is not updated in the uncommitted draft either.
Required: add an **Accessibility** row (and coordinate the **Product** row with AI-0353), update every "seven-row"/"seven review records" reference, and make the acceptance criteria and independent-review gate count the full set. The row evidence must cite this review and the accepted accessibility contract. Do not mark the row Approved until H2-H7 and M1-M4 close.

**H2. Accepted accessibility contracts are omitted and accepted obligations are reopened as an open point.**

## Low (track or fix opportunistically)

- **L1. Terminology/section placement.** "Accessibility and privacy" appears only under Avatar (L940), which makes the whole headed surface's accessibility obligations look avatar-specific. Move the Core-baseline obligations to a top-level section and distinguish "Core accessibility baseline (ADR 0016/W-134)" from "media accessibility obligations" so "accessibility baseline" is not confused with the draft candidate document.

1. Add the Accessibility P0 row (and the Product row, coordinated with AI-0353), update the seven-row wording, and make the independent-review gate count the full set.
2. Cite ADR 0016 Boundary 3 and the accepted W-134 accessibility extraction contract as normative sources, affected contracts, and references; state that the headed design consumes the Core baseline and weakens none of it.

5. Define synchronized captions and an inspectable transcript, with the Headed Agent as presentation owner, the media extension kept transcript-free, the same redacted text, and R3 retention.
6. Define avatar alternative content and state equivalence so no required information is conveyed only by the avatar or animation.
7. Define accessible media controls (labels, roles, states, keyboard/AT operation, stop/replay, captions/transcript) and preserve no-autoplay.
8. Extend presentation-never-authority to the accessibility projection and AT actions; no AT action may grant, approve, or bypass Core authorization, and the projection never reaches the Event Bus.

- A headed surface could ship pointer-only or with no screen-reader semantics while the P0 table appears complete, because accessibility is not a gate row.

P0-row recommendation: **NEEDS-FIX; keep the Accessibility row Pending.** Re-review the committed corrected candidate (and the corrected P0 table) before recording any approval. {"content":"VERDICT: NEEDS-FIX (Core / future bittyd P0 row). Final Core sign-off remains CONDITIONAL on an accepted bitty#2546 contract; this note is not a sign-off and authorizes no implementation.

Review base: bitty-ai-docs main 1243a14; candidate `agent/headed-agent-contracts-candidate.md` at 5d63ffc (#303, unchanged through main). The corrections branch `ai-0347/docs-p0-corrections` has no commits beyond main yet, so this is a pre-corrections review; re-review is required after it lands.

WHAT HOLDS (no finding):

- Presentation-never-authority, panel-not-session, no model I/O in Core, no credential exposure, and no `wheel.*` dependency are compatible with ADR-0013, the accepted Panel Runtime RFC, the accepted IPC/Agent RFC, and the AI Architecture SMO-2 direction.
- Consent default-deny, no bundled admin grant, revocation, and fresh re-grant match IPC RFC "Agent auth, consent, and streaming".
- `stop` maps cancellation to the accepted `Completed`/`Failed` AgentSession states without adding a third state; consistent with the IPC RFC.
- The `bitty-agent` layering claim is accurate: Core's graph test forbids `bitty-agent`/`bitty-agent-api` edges (`bitty/crates/bitty-terminal/tests/verify_w147_small_core_graph.rs`), and `bitty-ai-runtime` consumes `bitty-agent-api` at rev `a8e4112`.

P0 FINDINGS (blocking):
P0-1 Accepted Event Bus is missing and effectively redefined.
Evidence: candidate L145 "Event Bus ... (planned; not implemented here)"; L632-643 topic families; L653-654 Core "reserves ... `session.*`, `panel.*`, `tool.approval.*`, `tool.result.*`"; L471 non-lossy control class; L1288 says Core panel and Event Bus "would need its own accepted contract".
Accepted: `bitty-terminal-docs/specifications/panel-runtime-rfc.md` (accepted 2026-09-14) §Event Bus defines `owner.name:topic` (<=64 bytes), 8 KiB payload, per-sub 64 / per-panel 1024 events + 256 KiB / global 8192 + 2 MiB, DropOldest v1 default, no ordering across panels or topics, and "a bus topic never escapes a Window without an explicit cross-window or cross-process transport RFC; the v1 scope is single-process, single-window only"; `RFC-OQ-4` (exact bus topic taxonomy) remains open. `bitty-docs/docs/decisions/rfcs/***REDACTED***.md` (accepted 2026-10-07) fixes `panel.*` as the capability family (`panel.provider`, `panel.create`, `panel.focus`, `panel.overlay`) and keeps `DropOldest` for queued generation-N events.
Impact: per-session sequencing, non-lossy control classes, and cross-process attachment streaming cannot be assumed on the accepted bus; `panel.*` collides with the accepted capability family. Either align with the accepted bus or declare a new Core transport contract.

P0-2 Session authority conflates bittyd Session, AgentSession, and a new headed session, and is mis-routed.
Evidence: candidate L131 `bittyd` "future, undecided"; L318-320 "whether the durable session record and generation issuance live in Core or `bitty-ai`, remain open"; L1328 routes "Session authority split" to `OQ-061`; no citation of bitty#2546, ADR-0019, or the bittyd requirements candidate.
Accepted/direction: `OQ-061` is agent identity domains and panel projection, not session-host authority, and remains Open. ADR-0019 (accepted 2026-10-22) D1/D2 advances bittyd to the v0.2.0 slice with session-grained attach/detach, service API versioning, and no persistence across restart. bitty#2546 (OPEN, v0.2.0) required decisions 1-6 define session ownership, lifecycle, API/trust boundary, adapter, crash/reattach, and platform cells, and require the contract to be reusable by the future headed Agent plugin. `bitty-terminal-docs/specifications/bittyd-session-host-requirements-candidate.md` R-B09 records bittyd as the only writer of registry/lifecycle/generation/attach-count/lease/last-seen; D-03 keeps generation vs state revision open.
Impact: Core cannot tell whether `start` creates a bittyd session, an `AgentSession`, or an application handle; the "Core or bitty-ai" framing omits bittyd, bitty-execution, and bitty-agent. Re-route to bitty#2546 + ADR-0019, name the three session concepts, and keep final sign-off conditional on #2546.

P0-3 Core execution ownership conflicts with accepted ADR-0016 Boundary 1.
Evidence: candidate L199 Core owns "process/PTY supervision"; L591-594 "`tool.started` — Core starts an authorized execution"; L621 "The approval ledger, the verdict, and the execution record are Core-owned"; L1148 "Tool approval, execution, result | Owner of ledger and execution".
Accepted: `bitty-docs/docs/decisions/adrs/***REDACTED***.md` (accepted 2026-10-02) Boundary 1 moves the AI-agnostic execution supervisor (task lifecycle/spawn-time lifetime, cancellation execution, PTY and process resource management, structured outcome, bounded output, recovery) to `bitty-execution` under W-132; Core retains PTY ownership, permission/resource enforcement for observe/read_output/write_input/signal/cancel/attach/transfer, host-side generation fencing, and the AI-agnostic typed execution bridge; semantic task work stays with bitty-ai.
Impact: correct Core to "authorizes and fences", with bitty-execution as supervisor and bitty-ai as semantic owner; otherwise the candidate silently absorbs an accepted extraction.

P0-4 Generation axes are not mapped to accepted GenerationId/panel generation; attachment can outlive panel generation.
Evidence: candidate L396-410 defines session and attachment generations and binds consent/elevation to the session generation; L401 says the split remains open; L1141 "Session handle and generation | Transport only; durable identity placement open"; L748-750 allows several attachments per panel.
Accepted: ADR-0013 `Session` and `GenerationId` (fencing for reloads/leases/handoffs, scoped under the fenced object); Panel Runtime RFC `(PanelId, generation)` with `StaleHandle`; `specifications/execution-projection-binding-candidate.md` `Execution (id + generation) <-> Surface (id + generation)` and "Panel rebuilt (new generation)" fails the old binding closed; AI Architecture AG-2 binds agent levels to `(AgentId, generation)` (draft).
Impact: attachment identity is not tied to `(PanelId, generation)`, so a stale attachment can keep a stream after panel dispose/rebuild. Map session/attachment generations to `GenerationId`/panel generation or explicitly define a separate fence and its composition.

P0-5 An "open" point is silently decided: Core owns the session-generation sequence.
Evidence: candidate L423-430 "The Core owner owns the session-generation sequence. One Core-designated sequencer assigns a monotonically increasing sequence number per session generation at commit, before queue admission"; contradicted by L1328 and L1141, which leave generation issuance/record placement open.
Impact: this is a new Core mechanism asserted as settled; it also creates a sequence outside accepted IPC `seq` and the accepted bus. Mark it proposed Core contract work under #2546 or remove it from settled claims.

P1 FINDINGS (major):

- P1-1 Consent/elevation: candidate binds consent/elevation to the session generation (L407-410, L1056-1065); IPC RFC (accepted 2026-08-29) grants are per `(UID, AgentId)`, instance-scoped, survive restarts, with immediate revocation. Add an explicit "grant vs per-session elevation ticket" mapping; if it narrows accepted grants it is a contract amendment.
- P1-2 Panel lifecycle: accepted lifecycle is Declared -> Created -> Mounted -> Focused -> Suspended -> Disposed; suspend is invisibility without destroying attachment; panel identity is accepted, not "planned" (implementation is what is missing). The candidate's attachment states are broadly compatible, but "one panel may host several attachments in separate surfaces" extends the accepted panel model and needs a Core panel contract.
- P1-3 bittyd staging/resume: ADR-0019 accepted the v0.2.0 staging; "future, undecided" and "no v1.0 bittyd binary" understate it. Candidate `resume` ("session is retained") must be scoped to live detach/reattach; restart persistence is outside the v0.2.0 slice.
- P1-4 attach/takeover vs accepted panel lease: OQ-083 is accepted (panel lease direction Idle/Occupied, acquire/release/handoff) and is not cited. "Current owner ... authorizes the handoff" needs the bittyd owner-client/operator authority model and must not let a client grant a different principal control.
- P1-5 Ordering/non-lossy control: candidate L456-457 and L471 promise per-session-generation order and non-lossy control; the accepted bus says no ordering across panels/topics with DropOldest, and AI Architecture SMO-1 says events ride the accepted IPC bus with DropOldest. State the transport (IPC stream vs panel bus) and amend or narrow.
- P1-6 Missing Core contract references: L1288 says Core panel/Event Bus "would need its own accepted contract" although the Panel Runtime RFC is accepted; add rows/links for Panel Runtime RFC, RFC-0006, ADR-0013, ADR-0016, ADR-0019, OQ-058/OQ-083, bitty#2546, and the bittyd requirements candidate.

P2 FINDINGS (minor):

- P2-1 "panel ... (planned)" and "Event Bus (planned)" conflate contract acceptance with implementation status; accepted contracts exist.
- P2-2 `panel.*` reused as a bus topic namespace collides with the accepted `panel.*` capability family; use `owner.name:topic` and mark input to RFC-OQ-4.
- P2-3 L688-692 says the execution-projection binding "continues to govern"; it is a candidate document, not accepted. Mark candidate status in the affected-contracts table (currently "No change").
- P2-4 Media/GPU: cite ADR-0016 Boundary 2 (graphics decode/processing to bitty-graphics) and Boundary 5 (platform services) so "Core host integration" is not read as Core rendering/decoding.
- P2-5 Presentation "tiers A-D" collide with ADR-0002 platform Tier 1-3; call them presentation profiles.

RE-REVIEW CONDITIONS:

1. Re-read the corrected candidate after `ai-0347/docs-p0-corrections` lands; verify P0-1..P0-5 and P1-1..P1-6 are resolved in text and no new Core claim is silently added.
2. After bitty#2546 is accepted, verify exact alignment: session fields, generation vs state revision, attach lease and role, abort/stop authority, daemon stop/drain, stale-instance/stale-generation behavior, service API version, and platform cells.
3. Verify open-point routing: session authority -> #2546; panel lease -> OQ-083; bus taxonomy -> RFC-OQ-4; no remaining "Core owner owns ..." assertion in an open area.
4. Confirm final Core sign-off only after #2546 acceptance and a corrected-candidate re-review. Do not mark AI-0350 or AI-0347 complete from this review.

Impact: correct Core to "authorizes and fences", with bitty-execution as supervisor and bitty-ai as semantic owner; otherwise the candidate silently absorbs an accepted extraction.

P0-4 Generation axes are not mapped to accepted GenerationId/panel generation; attachment can outlive panel generation.

Accepted: ADR-0013 `Session` and `GenerationId` (fencing for reloads/leases/handoffs, scoped under the fenced object); Panel Runtime RFC `(PanelId, generation)` with `StaleHandle`; `specifications/execution-projection-binding-candidate.md` `Execution (id + generation) <-> Surface (id + generation)` and "Panel rebuilt (new generation)" fails the old binding closed; AI Architecture AG-2 binds agent levels to `(AgentId, generation)` (draft).

Evidence: candidate L423-430 "The Core owner owns the session-generation sequence. One Core-designated sequencer assigns a monotonically increasing sequence number per session generation at commit, before queue admission"; contradicted by L1328 and L1141, which leave generation issuance/record placement open.
Impact: this is a new Core mechanism asserted as settled; it also creates a sequence outside accepted IPC `seq` and the accepted bus. Mark it proposed Core contract work under #2546 or remove it from settled claims.

P1 FINDINGS (major):

- P1-1 Consent/elevation: candidate binds consent/elevation to the session generation (L407-410, L1056-1065); IPC RFC (accepted 2026-08-29) grants are per `(UID, AgentId)`, instance-scoped, survive restarts, with immediate revocation. Add an explicit "grant vs per-session elevation ticket" mapping; if it narrows accepted grants it is a contract amendment.

## High findings (blocking for the AI row)

**H-AI1. Routing-snapshot ownership is misassigned; accepted R1 splits publication from registry.**
Evidence: candidate L244 gives `headed.routing` the AI owner alone; L321-322 says "`bitty-ai` owns ... routing snapshot"; L1143 says "AI: Owner of resolution and routing snapshot"; L1279 says R1 is "Consumed unchanged ... ownership proof". Accepted R1 `architecture/execution-ownership-r1.md` L418-441 assigns **Core** publication authority (derives/publishes the exact canonical projection, mints the monotonic `snapshot_version` and never-reused identity, owns invalidation) and **the helper** the authoritative populated `ProviderRegistry`, validation, byte-for-byte equality, and opaque proof after acknowledgement. L496-505 makes `ai.provider_list` the only strict target and says strict use is not enabled. Required: `headed.routing` owners = AI owner (resolution/registry/proof) + Core owner (publication/version/invalidation); split the matrix cell; stop saying AI owns the routing snapshot; cite the proof/acknowledgement gate. AI ownership of routing _resolution_ itself is consistent with Provider plugin boundary L570-573 ("model-system abstraction and policy belong to `bitty-ai` Core") and BA-2 L1052; the defect is the snapshot ownership, not routing.

**H-AI2. Per-turn routing pin contradicts the accepted lifecycle and the "No change" claim.**
Evidence: candidate L552-555 pins a routing snapshot version/digest "for the turn and associated with the session generation"; L1279 says R1 is consumed unchanged. Accepted R1 L468-494: a changed projection supersedes the prior one; any registry/capability/context/cost/alias mutation invalidates the proof before strict use; missing, stale, future, replayed, duplicate, superseded, wrong-domain, wrong-digest, or projection-mismatched publications fail closed, with no fallback. A turn-pinned snapshot must be invalidated on mutation. Required: either remove per-turn pinning, or state that it is a **new consumer rule** (not "No change"), that a mutation invalidates the pin and fails the turn closed, and that a fresh publication requires a new pin; add a negative test. Also L521-531 still accepts an "alias" in the request; accepted R1 L327-333 and L776-778 forbid alias-dependent strict behavior until a separate accepted alias projection. (Security PX-1553 P1-1 overlaps; fix in the same pass.)

**H-AI3. "Core-owned" mislabels the provider boundary's `bitty-ai` Core.**
Evidence: candidate terminology L130 defines **Core** as the terminal platform; L108-112 calls the Provider plugin boundary's privacy classes, provider descriptor, and secret invariant "Core-owned"; the Provider plugin boundary L570-573 says "model-system abstraction and policy belong to `bitty-ai` Core; ... the contract, registry, and policy stay in Core", and L98-148 lists the `ModelProvider` interface, descriptor, capability vocabulary, selection/routing, fallback, budget, streaming, errors, and registry protocol as that surface. Under the candidate's own "Core = terminal" vocabulary, L108-112 would assign the descriptor and capability/privacy vocabulary to terminal Core. Required: use `bitty-ai` Core for those surfaces; add an explicit ownership-matrix row "provider descriptor / capability / privacy-class vocabulary = `bitty-ai` owner", with terminal Core limited to scopes, transport, credential storage, and consent enforcement; reserve "Core" for terminal Core.

**M-AI2. `bitty-agent-api` dependency is overclaimed.**

Required: say "test-only, report-only dev-dependency; production code does not depend on `bitty-agent` or its state machine"; name the runtime's own `AgentSession` and `Canceled`; do not imply accepted vocabulary convergence. **M-AI4. `AssetRef` is a shared contract, not AI-only.**

Evidence: candidate L1328 routes "Session authority split" to `OQ-061` as primary; `bitty-docs/docs/decisions/open-questions.md` L109 defines OQ-061 as agent identity-domain separation and panel projection, not durable session handle/generation issuance/reconnect. Evidence: candidate L367-373 maps `stop` to the accepted `Completed`/`Failed` terminal state with cancellation attribution and says it does not add a third accepted state; `bitty-ai/crates/bitty-ai-runtime/src/session.rs` L208-219 defines `Active/Completed/Failed/Canceled`, and L402-412 makes cancellation a terminal `Canceled` in the runtime. Required: add a two-level outcome table (session terminal state vs media/job outcome) and an explicit `Canceled` -> accepted-terminal mapping; do not imply the runtime state is the accepted state. **L-AI1. "Accepted state machine carried by the crate" overstates implementation acceptance.**
Evidence: candidate L315-318; `bitty-agent/crates/bitty-agent/src/session.rs` L21 marks the lifecycle "draft, not normative"; the AIQ note at `product/ai-unresolved-questions.md` L788 calls it an accepted contract with implementation not yet verified. **L-AI2. AI event vocabulary and viseme vocabulary are new ownership claims.**
Evidence: candidate L132/L200/L913-916 assign AI the AI-facing event vocabulary and the viseme identifier vocabulary; Multimodal L325-335 only says "AI emits `GenerationStarted`/`GenerationProgress`/`GenerationCompleted`" and does not assign viseme ownership. Required: label both as new AI-owned candidate vocabularies with no upstream acceptance, and route them to AI-owner acceptance in affected contracts/open points.

**L-AI3. Budget wording could imply a separate AI budget.**
Evidence: candidate L1155 says "AI and media-job budgets"; AI Architecture MP-9 L117 charges model I/O against the same per-client quotas as IPC/MCP and says no separate model-specific RC; R1 L254-259 says terminal-side per-client quotas plus helper-side pre-I/O gates, with usage reported, never self-granted. Evidence: candidate L18-24 says only the IPC/Agent RFC and the scoped routing binding are "cited as accepted contracts", but later cites accepted ADR-0002 and ADR-0008 decisions (L1332, L1337) and the normative security corpus. {"content":"AI-0352 plugin-ecosystem P0 review — verdict: **NEEDS-FIX**

**Scope and version.** Reviewed `bitty-ai-docs/agent/headed-agent-contracts-candidate.md` on `main` at `1243a14` (candidate last changed in `5d63ffc`, PR #303). The `ai-0347/docs-p0-corrections` worktree contains an uncommitted 599-insertion/293-deletion rewrite of the same file; that work is **not** reviewed here and some findings below may already be in flight. No edits, commits, pushes, or PRs were made by this reviewer. Review-only; AI-0352 and AI-0347 are not completed.

**Verdict.** The candidate correctly avoids inventing a plugin manifest and explicitly names `bitty-plugins-docs` as owner of the plugin platform, manifest, capability, and packaging contracts. It does not, however, disposition plugin packaging and media-extension ownership correctly: it treats a native media surface as a plugin package the accepted plugin platform cannot express, does not reconcile with the existing `ai-panel` split target, assigns AI plugin ownership to `bitty-plugins`, and omits the AI extension capability catalog the plugin would need. The P0 row cannot sign off on the current text.

## P1 — blocking for plugin-ecosystem sign-off

### P1-1. Media extension is treated as a plugin-ecosystem package with no accepted platform category

**Evidence (candidate).** `agent/headed-agent-contracts-candidate.md:136` defines a media extension as an "optional, separately packaged implementation of audio playback, decoding, 2D rendering, avatar rigging, or 3D presentation"; `:204` gives it "Audio device playback, media decoding, 2D rendering, 3D rigging, and GPU presentation behind a declared capability"; `:936` calls the 3D renderer a "separately packaged media extension with its own capability declaration"; `:1289` labels the affected contract "Plugin packaging for media extensions"; `:1329` makes "media extension packaging" blocked by the plugin packaging row.
**Evidence (authoritative).** The accepted `bitty-plugins-docs/specifications/plugin-platform-rfc.md:328-332` says "Native in-process plugins remain forbidden (R-017); the capability model assumes the restricted-VM runtime and confers nothing on native payloads." The accepted plugin UI surface (`:431-436`) allows declarative primitives only — "No shaders, pipelines, glyph injection, native windows, or global-coordinate drawing." `bitty-plugins-docs/extensibility/plugin-system.md:140-144` puts direct `wgpu::Device`/`wgpu::Queue`/texture access outside the initial plugin boundary; `:150-152` requires one isolated Lua VM per plugin with native module loading denied. The proposed `bitty-plugins-docs/packaging/plugin-reuse-and-providers.md:502-510` defers native helpers to post-1.0, and `:551-556` says FFmpeg-style decode is bounded and receives "no GPU, window, PTY, or host-Rust handles"; `:761-764` says the host owns one realization of the media primitive; `:779-780` says "No window/GPU object leaks to a plugin or helper." The accepted capability table (`plugin-platform-rfc.md:300-311`) has no audio/GPU/media family.
**Why it matters.** A future implementation task could read the ownership matrix as authorizing a native GPU/audio plugin, contradicting R-017 and the no-GPU-leak rules, or route media packaging to `bitty-plugins` when the established path is a Core-owned extension component (`bitty-graphics` is a "bounded graphics decode extension" with placement/upload validation in Core; `bitty-a11y` and `bitty-platform-services` are Core-owned installable `bitty-component.toml` components). The candidate's own P0 row would then be dispositioned against the wrong category.
**Required correction.** Define "media extension" as an owner-pending category, not a package class. State that (a) media decode/render/audio cannot be a v1 Lua plugin, (b) Layer 4 native helpers are post-1.0 and exclude GPU/window/PTY handles, (c) the existing Core extension-component path (`bitty-component.toml`, per-target digest, Core descriptor/placement/upload validation) is the established native-surface route, and (d) the packaging owner is Core/terminal-platform unless `bitty-plugins` accepts a new category. Split "plugin packaging for media extensions" out of the plugin packaging row.

### P1-2. The packaging row conflates identity, package category, distribution, and signing, and omits `ai-panel`

**Evidence (candidate).** `:1329` asks: "Is the Headed Agent a Lua plugin, an out-of-process component, or a composed distribution? Who signs and updates it?" with owner "Plugin ecosystem owner", routing "Follow-up issue", blocking "Plugin packaging, media extension packaging".
**Evidence (authoritative).** The plugin platform has: an accepted Lua plugin package (`plugin-platform-rfc.md:108-113`); an **unaccepted** out-of-process plugin boundary with no supervisor, cross-process bus, or capability-token mapping (`bitty-plugins-docs/architecture/plugin-ipc-boundary.md:41-68`, `:180-188`, open items 2/4/7 at `:304-326`); distribution presets/collections as post-v1.0 candidates over the accepted Default Distribution RFC (`bitty-plugins-docs/product/plugin-roadmap.md:465-495`); and accepted package lifecycle/integrity/rollback with real signature and registry wiring still draft (`bitty-plugins-docs/packaging/package-lifecycle-rfc.md:29-43`, `:128-156`; `package-followup-rfc.md:35-38`, `:58-65`). The plugin ecosystem already records `ai-panel` as the agent panel surface: "split later (hybrid)", "blocked on the panel-provider contract and the `bitty-ai` surfaces and distribution question" (`bitty-plugins-docs/product/bundled-plugin-split-decision.md:230-237`); `docs/plugins/README.md:66` says "Later / Not started; AI surfaces move to the optional `bitty-ai` extension." The candidate never mentions `ai-panel`.
**Why it matters.** The P0 row could be closed with a new plugin identity that duplicates `ai-panel`; "composed distribution" is not a plugin-platform category; the out-of-process option is blocked on unaccepted transport/supervision contracts, not a free alternative; and signing/update already has an owner at contract level.
**Required correction.** Split the row into four decisions: (1) plugin identity — adopt `ai-panel` as successor/rename or record the new identity and the relationship; (2) package category — Lua plugin vs out-of-process participant (blocked on plugin IPC open items 2/4/7 and Panel Runtime cross-process transport) vs Core component; (3) distribution presence — install-time/featured/bundled/preset under the Default Distribution RFC; (4) signing/update — cite Package Lifecycle/Follow-up RFC and name only the publisher/key identity that remains. Cite `ai-panel` and the plugin-platform open items.

### P1-3. Plugin ownership conflicts with the workspace AI-plugin jurisdiction

**Evidence (candidate).** `:1130` says "Plugin ecosystem owner is `bitty-plugins-docs` plus the plugin repositories"; `:1329` assigns "Headed plugin identity and packaging" to the Plugin ecosystem owner.
**Evidence (authoritative).** Workspace `AGENTS.md:73-84`: `bitty-plugins` is the "plugin ecosystem **without AI**" and owns official **non-AI** plugins; `bitty-ai` owns "every AI-related Lua plugin. AI involvement wins over the plugins jurisdiction: an AI-flavored plugin belongs to `bitty-ai`, never `bitty-plugins`." The Headed Agent is defined by the candidate itself as AI composition/speech/avatar consuming `bitty-ai` (`:28-37`, `:202`).
**Why it matters.** The platform-contract owner and the plugin product owner are conflated. An AI plugin could be assigned to the wrong commander, and the P0 reviewer role would be read as an implementation-ownership transfer.
**Required correction.** Separate "plugin platform contract owner" (`bitty-plugins-docs`: manifest/capability/packaging) from "Headed Agent plugin product/implementation owner" (`bitty-ai` per workspace jurisdiction), with joint review only for the platform contract. {"content":"Product P0 re-review — AI-0353 (parent AI-0347), corrected revision 01a1ad4

Verdict: NEEDS-FIX

Scope and revision

- Reviewed commit `01a1ad4c8098e9d85005462180bc7cc800d78c72` on branch `ai-0347/docs-p0-corrections` (worktree `ai-0347-docs-p0-corrections`, branch head matches `origin/ai-0347/docs-p0-corrections`), PR #306, document `agent/headed-agent-contracts-candidate.md` (2620 lines).
- GitHub API was unreachable from this host (TLS handshake timeout), so PR metadata/checks were not re-read. The commit under review is the pushed branch head; the review is read-only. No files edited, no commit, push, or merge.
- Prior verdict `PX-1563` reviewed `main` at `1243a14`, before the product section existed. This note reviews the corrected candidate at `01a1ad4` and does not treat the earlier note as approval of this revision.
- AI-0353 and AI-0347 are not marked complete; the Product row remains `Pending — NEEDS-FIX`.

What the correction gets right

- **Gate (prior P1-1): closed.** The `P0 Review Sign-off` table is nine rows and includes Product and Accessibility (`L2506-2520`); all nine are `Pending — NEEDS-FIX`; the status block, security-review text, ownership matrix, and `TODO.md` all say nine and none is approved (`L25-32`, `L2071-2073`, `L2117`, `L2522-2525`; `TODO.md` diff in `01a1ad4`). D7 records the correction as discharged and the other six product decisions as open (`L190`, `L2395`).
- **Product thesis and v1 scope (prior P1-2): closed at the required level.** The new section `Product thesis and v1 placement` (`L99-191`) cites the accepted Product Vision anchor and gives a candidate thesis plus a candidate v1 scope table (`L101-134`). D1 explicitly names target user, minimum surface, milestone, and relation to the Wheel chat UI and terminal panes as the open decision (`L2389`). This satisfies the prior requirement of "a product-scope section or an explicit open point"; it does not decide D1, which is correct for a candidate.
- **Predecessor record (prior P1-3): substantially added.** `L136-160` records `bitty-terminal.ai-panel`, the 2026-09-30 removal (`bitty` CTX-0886), the accepted AI Surface Accepted Record, and the split-later hybrid. D5/P-1 keep identity open. One residual placement contradiction remains (P1-A below).
- **Recording/export/deletion (prior P1-5): closed.** The contract floor is separated from the product capability; D3 is explicit and conditional ("if the product offers them at all", `L133`); Tier C "later playback" now requires a declared retention class and explicit consent (`L1834`); Data rules state the floor and say the two are not in tension (`L1944-1949`).
- **Synthetic-speech disclosure (prior P2-3): closed.** Disclosure is mandatory and the minimum form is D2, not silently chosen (`L1457-1460`, `L2363`, `L2390`).
- **Consent surface (prior P2-1): closed.** The body fixes authorization/revocation semantics and leaves prompt placement/content, grant review/revocation UI, speech-versus-model egress distinction, and consent fatigue to D6 (`L1902-1929`, `L2394`).
- **Plugin identity (prior P2-2): mostly closed.** P-1 through P-4 separate identity, package category, distribution presence, and signing; "Headed Agent" is marked working name only (`L2397-2407`, `L368`). D5 remains over-broad (P1-A).
- **No implementation claim.** The document stays `draft`; it explicitly disclaims a headed surface, speech, avatar, provider loader, and panel implementation (`L14-32`, `L69-81`).

Findings

P1-A — D5 reopens the accepted repository placement of AI surfaces, and the body calls that placement an "assumption".

Evidence:

- Candidate `L153-157`: "This draft works from the assumption that placement is an optional `bitty-ai` extension, the recorded destination for AI surfaces and the jurisdiction where AI involvement wins, while the final product placement and user-facing name remain `D5`."
- Candidate `L2393` (D5): "Product placement and user-facing name: `ai-panel` successor identity, optional `bitty-ai` extension, and whether a distribution is offered. ... Open. This document's placement is a candidate, not an accepted product decision."
- The candidate itself states the accepted placement at `L140-141`: "AI surfaces move to the separate optional `bitty-ai` extension".
- Accepted record: `bitty-terminal-docs/specifications/ai-surface-accepted-record.md` `L29-33`: the `bitty-terminal.ai-panel` entry was removed and "AI surfaces move to the separate optional `bitty-ai` extension"; the record "applies to any future AI panel built on the generic primitives". `bitty-terminal-docs/product/vision.md` `L103-108` and `bitty-docs/docs/decisions/index.md` `L311-313` record the same accepted direction.

Impact: the accepted repository placement is presented as an assumption and then re-opened as D5. The Product owner is invited to re-decide something the accepted AI Surface Accepted Record and Product Vision already fix. D5 also overlaps P-1 (identity) and P-3 (distribution presence), so the decision boundary is unclear.

Fix: state that repository placement is fixed by the accepted AI Surface Accepted Record/Product Vision (optional `bitty-ai` extension); limit D5 to product identity and user-facing name; remove "assumption"; deduplicate distribution presence with P-3 and reconcile P-3's "bundled" option with the accepted optional-extension placement.

P1-B — Captions/transcript are labeled "accepted baseline obligations" with no accepted source, so the settled/open boundary is still wrong.

Evidence:

- Candidate `L2366`: "now that reduced motion, contrast, focus, announcements, and captions/transcript are accepted baseline obligations"; the same row says "ADR-0016 Boundary 3, `W-134`, RFC-0001, and RFC-0002 fix the baseline".
- Candidate D4 `L2392`: "The accepted baseline (ADR-0016, `W-134`, RFC-0001, RFC-0002) is not reopened."
- Candidate `L1664-1665`: captions plus transcript are "a baseline obligation whenever speech is presented".
- The candidate's own `Consumed accepted baseline` table (`L1572-1579`) lists ADR-0016 Boundary 3, `W-134`, RFC-0001, RFC-0002, OQ-078, and the P0 criteria, and does **not** list captions/transcript.
- Verification: a repository-wide search over `bitty-docs`, `bitty-terminal-docs`, and `bitty-ai-docs` Markdown found no accepted captions/transcript obligation; `W-134`, RFC-0001, RFC-0002, and the P0 acceptance criteria do not name captions or transcripts. The only occurrence of the concept outside this candidate is in the candidate itself.
- The security gate at `L2103` also folds captions/transcript into "meet the accepted baseline".

Impact: a candidate requirement is mislabeled as accepted. D4 ("beyond the accepted baseline") then cannot own the v1/post-v1 caption decision, and the document simultaneously treats captions as settled (always present) and as an open presentation-detail decision (`L2366`). This is the same settled/open defect prior P1-4 identified, narrowed to the caption/transcript part; the reduced-motion, contrast, focus, and announcement parts are now correctly tied to accepted sources.

Fix: describe captions/transcript as candidate v1 baseline requirements (or move them under D4) until an accepted speech/accessibility contract names them; align `L1664-1665`, `L2103`, `L2366`, and D4.

P2-A — "text and captions work at the lowest presentation class" contradicts the `P-D` class.

Evidence: candidate `L134` says "text and captions work at the lowest presentation class"; `L1835` defines `P-D` as "Headless or no presentation attachment ... no rendering, audio, or avatar resources". Captions cannot work at `P-D`. `P-C` is the lowest class with text and captions (`L1834`).

Fix: say text and captions work at `P-C`, the lowest attached presentation class, and that `P-D` remains headless.

P2-B — The split-later citation omits the 2026-09-30 supersession and reads as if the split is still pending.

Evidence: candidate `L144-148` cites the split-later hybrid; `L159-160` says "the `bitty-ai` surfaces and distribution questions that blocked the split remain open". The cited `bitty-plugins-docs/product/bundled-plugin-split-decision.md` `L25-32` explicitly says the 2026-09-30 removal "supersedes ... the split-later posture for `ai-panel` and `mail-panel`; the verdicts below are kept as the 2026-09-14 record."

Fix: state that the removal superseded the split-later posture, and that the remaining `bitty-ai` surfaces/distribution questions gate the successor, not "the split".

P2-C — Predecessor capabilities are not mapped to the candidate v1 scope.

Evidence: candidate `L145-146` says the predecessor's split target included a Lua chat UI, history, and commands; `L128` excludes "Chat transcript persistence" from v1; the v1 table does not mention history or commands. The document claims a "successor candidate" without saying which predecessor capabilities carry over, which are deferred, and which are D1/D5 decisions.

Fix: add a short capability mapping (chat composition, history, commands, approvals) to the placement paragraph or D1, or state explicitly that the successor does not inherit the predecessor's full surface.

P2-D — The thesis does not distinguish the surface from terminal agent panes.

Evidence: candidate `L113-118` distinguishes "not a replacement terminal, not the Wheel TUI, not a general chat client", but does not address an agent running in a terminal pane. D1 `L2389` defers the "relation to the Wheel chat UI and terminal panes". The thesis's value claim "without leaving the terminal host" is also true of a pane.

Fix: add one distinguishing sentence (for example, a panel composes session state, approvals, speech, and avatar across the workspace rather than emulating a terminal) or state explicitly that D1 owns this and the thesis makes no distinction yet.

P2-E — v1 speech output versus owner-pending playback.

Evidence: candidate `L130` offers "Optional speech output"; `L132` says "Core presentation primitives only; no v1 media package"; `L1419-1424` makes playback an owner-pending media presentation (Core extension component or post-1.0 native helper) and claims no Core audio implementation.

Fix: clarify whether v1 speech output depends on the owner-pending component or is itself post-v1; align the Speech and Media rows with the playback ownership statement.

Minor note (not a separate finding): D2 is correctly open, but the body's "in any exported metadata" (`L1457`) settles the export-metadata form while D2 lists "provenance metadata on exported assets" as part of the open minimum (`L2390`). Clarify that export metadata is a floor when export exists (D3), or move the wording under D2.

Product decisions still needed

- **D1** — Product thesis and v1 scope: target user, minimum surface (text/speech/avatar), milestone, and relation to the Wheel chat UI and terminal panes. Open; Product owner + `bitty-ai` owner. The candidate section and D1 record it, but it is not accepted.
- **D2** — Synthetic-speech disclosure minimum: spoken, visual, metadata-only, and provenance metadata on exported assets. Open; Security owner + Product owner. Disclosure itself is mandatory.
- **D3** — Record/export/delete rights and retention class offered by the v1 product, aligned with the fixed contract floor and the export-preview gate. Open; Core owner + Security owner + Product owner.
- **D4** — Accessibility floor beyond the accepted baseline. Open; Accessibility owner. P1-B must move captions/transcript to the correct side of the baseline first.
- **D5** — Product identity and user-facing name. Open; Product owner + `bitty-ai` owner. Repository placement is fixed by the accepted AI Surface Accepted Record; D5 should not reopen it (P1-A).
- **D6** — Consent surface: prompt placement/content, grant review and revocation UI, speech-versus-model egress distinction, and the consent-fatigue stance. Open; Product owner + Security owner.
- **D7** — Gate correction: discharged in this revision; nine rows, all pending.

Gate status

- Product row: `Pending — NEEDS-FIX (PX-1563 / AI-0353)`. This re-review records NEEDS-FIX; it does not approve the Product row.

## PASS (corrected items verified)

- AT adapter is not a principal; controlled action interface only; no grant/approve/Event Bus: L1719-1741; threat row L2080; security gate L2102. The adapter forwards bounded actions through Core's command registry and never publishes the projection, matching W-134 L323-368.

## High (blocking the row)

**H1. AT approval operability contradiction.** L1731-1735 says "An AT action cannot grant or approve … An AT 'activate' on an approval dialog may open or focus the decision surface but cannot record a verdict by itself"; L1757 and L2102 repeat "cannot approve." But L1637 requires keyboard equivalence for "Approve, deny, or defer … choose each verdict, confirm, cancel," and L1067 says the Headed Agent surface "collects the user's explicit decision." W-134 L323-351 defines the v1 controlled action as activation of a declared interactive node resolved through the command registry; an AT user activating the bound approval control is exactly that action. As written, a screen-reader user can open the dialog but cannot record a verdict, contradicting the keyboard-equivalence table and making approval inoperable by AT. Required: distinguish adapter autonomy from user action. The adapter cannot approve on its own; an explicit AT-generated activation of the bound decision control is user input that resolves through the Core authorization path and records the verdict only after the bound decision/confirmation. Apply the same wording at L1757 and L2102.

## Remaining findings

### High (blocking for the Architecture P0 row)

**H-A. The `bitty-ai` runtime session state set is misstated.**
Evidence: candidate L736 gives the runtime row as `Created`, `Running`, `WaitingToolResult`, `Completed`, `Failed`, `Canceled`; L712-714 says the runtime vocabulary has a terminal `Canceled`; L621-631 says the AI runtime defines its own `AgentSession` including `Canceled`. The actual runtime is `bitty-ai/crates/bitty-ai-runtime/src/session.rs` L208-219: `SessionState { Active, Completed, Failed, Canceled }`. The `Created`/`Running`/`WaitingToolResult`/`Completed`/`Failed` machine is the `bitty-agent` crate (`bitty-agent` `session.rs:23`), as the AI-0257 ledger itself records (`bitty-ai/crates/bitty-ai-runtime/tests/vocabulary_conformance.rs` L498-505: "runtime session.rs:210 Active/Completed/Failed/Canceled vs agent session.rs:23 Created/Running/WaitingToolResult/Completed/Failed"). The correction fuses the two vocabularies in the one table that is supposed to map them.
Required: use `Active`, `Completed`, `Failed`, `Canceled` for the runtime row, state the explicit mapping from the accepted RFC states (`Created`/`Running`/`WaitingToolResult` -> `Active`; `Completed`/`Failed` unchanged; cancellation -> `Canceled`), and keep the `bitty-agent` state set attributed to `bitty-agent`, not the runtime.

**H-B. The `bittyd` worker-binding generation is conflated with the application-level session generation.**
Evidence: candidate L608 says a `bittyd` session has "a worker-binding generation and a state revision"; L376 and L779 say the session generation fences approvals/consent and that "if `bittyd` owns that record, `bittyd` is the sole writer of the generation under `R-B09`." The bittyd consumer requirements define `generation` as the "Worker-binding counter; increments on each worker bind or rebind, never reused" (`bitty-terminal-docs/specifications/bittyd-session-host-requirements-candidate.md` L161-167, R-S16 L181-183), and attach/detach explicitly do not change it. The candidate uses the same word for a fence that changes on session `resume`/`takeover` (L754-755) and binds consent/elevation (L797). If the two are the same, a worker rebind rotates the consent fence and a controller handoff does not; if they are different, bittyd has no such field and the "sole writer" claim is incomplete. L544-546 also says the generation is "created by `start`" while L376/L779 leaves issuance to `bitty#2546`.
Required: define the application-level session generation as a distinct fence with its own issuer/record, or state explicitly that `bitty#2546` must add a separate `bittyd` field and that the worker generation is not it; replace "created by `start`" with "returned by `start`" and state the issuer-to-sequencer handoff for this fence. Keep `R-B09`'s worker-generation meaning intact.

**H-C. OQ-058/SMO delivery semantics and the IPC-versus-Panel-bus distinction remain unmapped.**
Evidence: `bitty-docs/docs/decisions/open-questions.md` L106 records OQ-058 as accepted with "delivery semantics (envelope identity, attribution, deadline, priority, dedup, cancellation, expiry)." `bitty-ai-docs/architecture/ai-architecture.md` L713 (SMO-1) says the events ride "the accepted IPC event bus (framing, per-queue budgets, `DropOldest`)" and carry `(AgentId, generation, kind)`. The accepted Panel Runtime RFC defines a different bus: host-mediated, single-process/single-window, explicitly "not an IPC TCP surface" (`bitty-terminal-docs/specifications/panel-runtime-rfc.md` L351-353, L428-432). The candidate cites OQ-058 only as topology/presentation (L220-223) and reduces it to four mandates (L1180-1184), omitting envelope identity, deadline, priority, dedup, and expiry. It then makes the Panel Event Bus observation-only and puts approvals/stop/tool results on a "session control stream defined by `headed.stream`" (L815-823, L1080-1082) without saying whether that stream is the SMO IPC path or a new transport. The accepted IPC RFC's non-lossy path is request/response and chunked streaming (`specifications/ipc-agent-rfc.md` L166-175, L499-516), not a durable sequenced control stream.
Required: distinguish the two buses by name; map the control stream to the accepted IPC event kinds/delivery semantics or state that it is a new `headed.stream` contract with its own accepted transport; add the SMO envelope/dedup/deadline/priority/expiry rules or cite them by section. This is the prior H5 requirement still unmet.

Core owns the artifact-reference contract"), L2056 ("Core ... owns the shared `AssetRef` contract"). The only source is the draft `bitty-ai-docs/providers/multimodal-inference-boundary.md` (`status: draft`; L274-290 candidate direction; L361 "AssetRef contract | Shared Core contract" is a proposal row). ADR-0016 Boundary 1 (L205) assigns "output retention and artifact reference mechanics" to `bitty-execution` and parks the exact shapes to `W-132`.

The `ai.provider` catalog is in `bitty-ai-docs/providers/capability-contribution-model.md` (`status: draft`, L170). L1789-1793 says "Every stored artifact names a retention class: `ephemeral`, `session`, or `explicit`" with per-class lifetimes. `bitty-ai-docs/architecture/context-retention-r3.md` L200-220 defines two candidate classes (consented digest-only usage rows; transient observation rows held in the bounded in-memory session); it does not define the `ephemeral`/`session`/`explicit` trio.

## Remaining findings

### High (blocking for the Architecture P0 row)

**H-A. The `bitty-ai` runtime session state set is misstated.**
Evidence: candidate L736 gives the runtime row as `Created`, `Running`, `WaitingToolResult`, `Completed`, `Failed`, `Canceled`; L712-714 says the runtime vocabulary has a terminal `Canceled`; L621-631 says the AI runtime defines its own `AgentSession` including `Canceled`. The actual runtime is `bitty-ai/crates/bitty-ai-runtime/src/session.rs` L208-219: `SessionState { Active, Completed, Failed, Canceled }`. The `Created`/`Running`/`WaitingToolResult`/`Completed`/`Failed` machine is the `bitty-agent` crate (`bitty-agent` `session.rs:23`), as the AI-0257 ledger itself records (`bitty-ai/crates/bitty-ai-runtime/tests/vocabulary_conformance.rs` L498-505: "runtime session.rs:210 Active/Completed/Failed/Canceled vs agent session.rs:23 Created/Running/WaitingToolResult/Completed/Failed"). The correction fuses the two vocabularies in the one table that is supposed to map them.
Required: use `Active`, `Completed`, `Failed`, `Canceled` for the runtime row, state the explicit mapping from the accepted RFC states (`Created`/`Running`/`WaitingToolResult` -> `Active`; `Completed`/`Failed` unchanged; cancellation -> `Canceled`), and keep the `bitty-agent` state set attributed to `bitty-agent`, not the runtime.

**H-B. The `bittyd` worker-binding generation is conflated with the application-level session generation.**
Evidence: candidate L608 says a `bittyd` session has "a worker-binding generation and a state revision"; L376 and L779 say the session generation fences approvals/consent and that "if `bittyd` owns that record, `bittyd` is the sole writer of the generation under `R-B09`." The bittyd consumer requirements define `generation` as the "Worker-binding counter; increments on each worker bind or rebind, never reused" (`bitty-terminal-docs/specifications/bittyd-session-host-requirements-candidate.md` L161-167, R-S16 L181-183), and attach/detach explicitly do not change it. The candidate uses the same word for a fence that changes on session `resume`/`takeover` (L754-755) and binds consent/elevation (L797). If the two are the same, a worker rebind rotates the consent fence and a controller handoff does not; if they are different, bittyd has no such field and the "sole writer" claim is incomplete. L544-546 also says the generation is "created by `start`" while L376/L779 leaves issuance to `bitty#2546`.
Required: define the application-level session generation as a distinct fence with its own issuer/record, or state explicitly that `bitty#2546` must add a separate `bittyd` field and that the worker generation is not it; replace "created by `start`" with "returned by `start`" and state the issuer-to-sequencer handoff for this fence. Keep `R-B09`'s worker-generation meaning intact.

**H-C. OQ-058/SMO delivery semantics and the IPC-versus-Panel-bus distinction remain unmapped.**
Evidence: `bitty-docs/docs/decisions/open-questions.md` L106 records OQ-058 as accepted with "delivery semantics (envelope identity, attribution, deadline, priority, dedup, cancellation, expiry)." `bitty-ai-docs/architecture/ai-architecture.md` L713 (SMO-1) says the events ride "the accepted IPC event bus (framing, per-queue budgets, `DropOldest`)" and carry `(AgentId, generation, kind)`. The accepted Panel Runtime RFC defines a different bus: host-mediated, single-process/single-window, explicitly "not an IPC TCP surface" (`bitty-terminal-docs/specifications/panel-runtime-rfc.md` L351-353, L428-432). The candidate cites OQ-058 only as topology/presentation (L220-223) and reduces it to four mandates (L1180-1184), omitting envelope identity, deadline, priority, dedup, and expiry. It then makes the Panel Event Bus observation-only and puts approvals/stop/tool results on a "session control stream defined by `headed.stream`" (L815-823, L1080-1082) without saying whether that stream is the SMO IPC path or a new transport. The accepted IPC RFC's non-lossy path is request/response and chunked streaming (`specifications/ipc-agent-rfc.md` L166-175, L499-516), not a durable sequenced control stream.
Required: distinguish the two buses by name; map the control stream to the accepted IPC event kinds/delivery semantics or state that it is a new `headed.stream` contract with its own accepted transport; add the SMO envelope/dedup/deadline/priority/expiry rules or cite them by section. This is the prior H5 requirement still unmet.

The bittyd consumer requirements define `generation` as the "Worker-binding counter; increments on each worker bind or rebind, never reused" (`bitty-terminal-docs/specifications/bittyd-session-host-requirements-candidate.md` L161-167, R-S16 L181-183), and attach/detach explicitly do not change it. The candidate uses the same word for a fence that changes on session `resume`/`takeover` (L754-755) and binds consent/elevation (L797). If the two are the same, a worker rebind rotates the consent fence and a controller handoff does not; if they are different, bittyd has no such field and the "sole writer" claim is incomplete. L544-546 also says the generation is "created by `start`" while L376/L779 leaves issuance to `bitty#2546`.
Required: define the application-level session generation as a distinct fence with its own issuer/record, or state explicitly that `bitty#2546` must add a separate `bittyd` field and that the worker generation is not it; replace "created by `start`" with "returned by `start`" and state the issuer-to-sequencer handoff for this fence. Keep `R-B09`'s worker-generation meaning intact.

**H-C. OQ-058/SMO delivery semantics and the IPC-versus-Panel-bus distinction remain unmapped.**
Evidence: `bitty-docs/docs/decisions/open-questions.md` L106 records OQ-058 as accepted with "delivery semantics (envelope identity, attribution, deadline, priority, dedup, cancellation, expiry)." `bitty-ai-docs/architecture/ai-architecture.md` L713 (SMO-1) says the events ride "the accepted IPC event bus (framing, per-queue budgets, `DropOldest`)" and carry `(AgentId, generation, kind)`. The accepted Panel Runtime RFC defines a different bus: host-mediated, single-process/single-window, explicitly "not an IPC TCP surface" (`bitty-terminal-docs/specifications/panel-runtime-rfc.md` L351-353, L428-432). The candidate cites OQ-058 only as topology/presentation (L220-223) and reduces it to four mandates (L1180-1184), omitting envelope identity, deadline, priority, dedup, and expiry. It then makes the Panel Event Bus observation-only and puts approvals/stop/tool results on a "session control stream defined by `headed.stream`" (L815-823, L1080-1082) without saying whether that stream is the SMO IPC path or a new transport. The accepted IPC RFC's non-lossy path is request/response and chunked streaming (`specifications/ipc-agent-rfc.md` L166-175, L499-516), not a durable sequenced control stream.
Required: distinguish the two buses by name; map the control stream to the accepted IPC event kinds/delivery semantics or state that it is a new `headed.stream` contract with its own accepted transport; add the SMO envelope/dedup/deadline/priority/expiry rules or cite them by section. ## New P1 — real blocker (PX-1581 confirmed)

**The AT approval path is not enforceable as written.** L1912-1920 now says an "explicit activation by the user" of a bound decision control, "delivered through AT as the v1 controlled action class," is user input and can record a verdict after "the bound decision and its confirmation step complete." L1943 and L2313 require a "programmatic-activation rejection" and a "user-activation approval path" test, and L2291 says explicit user activation is the only approval-capable AT input.

There is no trust anchor distinguishing that activation from a compromised adapter's programmatic request:

- L1902-1903: the adapter is not a principal, is not trusted by location, and is not trusted because it is first-party.
- L1904-1908: an AT action is a typed request through the Core controlled action interface; the host revalidates only element identity and projection generation. That is an integrity check on the target, not proof of human activation.
- W-134 L323-351 defines the v1 controlled action as adapter-forwarded activation of a declared interactive node; it supplies no user-gesture authentication, no caller attestation, and no unforgeable activation token.
- L1919-1920 says "programmatically invoking the control is not user input and cannot approve," but this is an assertion, not an enforcement. A compromised adapter can send the same typed activation and claim it is user-originated; Core has no independent signal.
- The "confirmation step" at L1918-1919 is undefined. If it is another AT action, it is equally forgeable; if it is a Core-owned keyboard/pointer event, the document must say so and exclude the adapter from minting or forwarding it.
- L2182-2184 still says unconditionally that an AT adapter "cannot approve or grant," which contradicts L1915-1919. One of the two statements must change.

Impact: a compromised or malicious AT adapter can approve a tool call, speech egress, or panel lease. That is the exact authority the AT section says it cannot have, and it invalidates the PX-1575 security approval. PX-1581 is correct: this is a real blocker, not a wording preference. The "programmatic-activation rejection" gate cannot establish the property without a defined trust anchor.

## Exact fix required

Choose one of the following; both are acceptable to the security finding, but the document must state the mechanism and test it.

**Option A (preferred; preserves AT activation): Core-minted user-activation proof.**

- Approval-capable controls are a separate action class. An AT adapter may focus, announce, scroll, open, or select a proposed verdict, but cannot record the verdict.
- A verdict is recorded only when the Core authorization path consumes a **single-use user-activation proof** minted by Core's trusted input path from an OS-delivered keyboard or pointer event on the focused bound decision control. The proof binds the principal, session generation, approval request identity, canonical argument digest, target, element identity, projection generation, and expiry; it is consumed exactly once and fails closed when missing, expired, replayed, mismatched, or adapter-supplied.
- The proof is never exposed to, minted by, or accepted from an AT adapter, plugin, or media component. Adapter-supplied "user activation" flags or confirmation strings are ignored.
- If the platform cannot deliver a Core-observable activation event, AT activation is non-approving; the documented keyboard confirmation path is the fallback and the adapter must not claim approval capability.
- Update L1912-1920, L2182-2184, L1943, L2291, and L2313. Add tests: compromised adapter sends a valid current-generation activation with a forged user-activation claim -> typed denial, no verdict; proof replay/stale/mismatch fails; proof is consumed once; a real keyboard activation succeeds once; no proof fails closed.

**Option B (minimum, docs-only; secure but less convenient).**

- Make AT activation of decision controls non-approving: open, focus, announce, scroll, or select only. The verdict is recorded only by a Core-observed keyboard or pointer activation through the trusted input path.
- Document the screen-reader keyboard confirmation path and require the dialog to announce it; do not require pointer-only input. Remove the L1915-1919 claim that AT activation records a verdict, keep L2182-2184, and update L1943, L2291, and L2313.
- Add the compromised-adapter test: an AT activation of a decision control never records a verdict; the keyboard path records it once; a stale element fails closed.

**Status sync required with either option.**

- L31-37 says the second-pass re-review approved Security and "no row other than Security is approved." L2274-2284 says the security design review was completed at `01a1ad4` with `APPROVE (design review)` under `PX-1575`. L2798 records `Approved (design review, PX-1575)`. PX-1581 reviewed `3091977` and says the prior approval does not carry forward. After PX-1581, the Security row must read `Pending — NEEDS-FIX (PX-1581)`, the Security section must record the `3091977` disposition, and the intro must not claim a Security approval. The Accessibility row must record PX-1573 plus PX-1581/this note and remain pending.

## Exact remaining blockers

1. **AT user-activation trust boundary** — Option A or Option B above. Without it, a compromised adapter can approve through the bounded action interface, and the Accessibility row cannot approve the path.
2. **Security sign-off status sync** — L31-37, L2274-2284, and L2798 still claim PX-1575 approval; PX-1581 withdrew it at `3091977`. Update before any disposition.
3. **Low polish (non-blocking)** — L1763 still says "Role `text` region"; normalize to role `text` inside a named `group` if the W-134 vocabulary is intended literally. This does not block the row.
